author: 404secnotfound
description: Member-server side of the Silver Ticket absence correlation. Flags Kerberos network logons (4624 LogonType 3 or 8) by user accounts on the server that receives the ticket. A Silver Ticket is forged with the service account key and presented straight to the service, so the DCs log no 4769 for that user and service. This rule surfaces the candidate logons; the correlation in the note supplies the fidelity. The single-event TargetDomainName markers live in forged_ticket_domain_field_anomaly.
falsepositives: Every normal Kerberos network logon. Do not deploy as a standalone alert.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND (LogonType=3 OR LogonType=8) AND AuthenticationPackageName='Kerberos') AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Silver Ticket Hunting Trigger (Kerberos Network Logon)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunts for the moment a Windows host falls back from DNS to multicast name resolution. When a DNS query for a single-label name (a mistyped share such as \\fileservr) or a name under the internal AD domain returns name error (NXDOMAIN, status 9003), the resolver then tries LLMNR and NBT-NS, which is the window Responder and Inveigh poison. On its own this is ordinary typo and stale-shortcut noise, so the rule is informational. Its value is as the first half of a join with llmnr_response_from_unexpected_host for the same host and name, and as a list of names to register in DNS so the fallback stops happening.
falsepositives: Mistyped UNC paths, stale shortcuts and mapped drives to decommissioned servers (the expected bulk of hits; register or clean up the names)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-DNS Client Events/Operational' AND ((EventID=3008 AND QueryStatus=9003) AND (QueryName REGEXP '^[^.]+$' OR QueryName LIKE '%.PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((QueryName='wpad' OR QueryName='isatap') OR (QueryName LIKE 'wpad.%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE 'isatap.%' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: DNS Client Name Error for an Internal or Single-Label Name (LLMNR Fallback Precondition)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for the noPac chain correlation. A 4781 where the old name has no trailing "$" and the new name has one, the step where noPac renames the spoofed computer account back to its original name after obtaining a TGT for the DC short name. Not an alert on its own.
falsepositives: Rare renames of user objects to names ending in "$"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4781 AND NewTargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' AND OldTargetUserName REGEXP '[^$]$')
title: Account Renamed From a Plain Name Back to a Computer Name (noPac Restore Step, Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for step 2 of the ESC8 relay chain (adcs_esc8_web_enrollment_relay.yml). Matches a 4624 network logon (LogonType 3) with NTLM on the Certification Authority host where the account is a Domain Controller machine account. An NTLM relay from a coerced DC to AD CS web enrollment produces exactly this logon on the CA, with the attacker's address in IpAddress.
falsepositives: A CA co-located with a Domain Controller, or a DC falling back to NTLM because of a Kerberos fault
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND AuthenticationPackageName='NTLM' AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\') AND Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_SERVER\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\')
title: Domain Controller Account NTLM Network Logon on the CA Host (Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting trigger. Surfaces inbound Kerberos delegation logons (4624 LogonType 3, ImpersonationLevel Delegation) to unconstrained-delegation hosts. These occur routinely on delegation-configured servers, so this is not a standalone alert. The real abuse signal is a privileged account (or DC machine account, coerced via printerbug/PetitPotam) delegating to an attacker-controlled unconstrained host, then TGT extraction via Rubeus tgtdeleg / monitor. Operationalise as a per-host count anomaly in the SIEM. PDF reference: "Get-NetComputer -Unconstrained".
falsepositives: Every delegation-configured app server. Do not alert standalone; baseline first.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND (ImpersonationLevel LIKE '\%\%1841' ESCAPE '\' OR ImpersonationLevel='Delegation') AND AuthenticationPackageName='Kerberos')
title: Unconstrained Delegation Host Caching TGTs (Hunting)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting trigger for the Golden Ticket absence correlation. Flags 4769 TGS requests using RC4 for non-machine services. A forged TGT is never issued by the KDC, so the user presenting it has no matching 4768 from the same source address within the TGT lifetime. Single-event detection is not high-fidelity because legacy RC4 service accounts produce the same signal; the fidelity comes from the native correlation described in the note. AES-based forgeries (Diamond and Sapphire tickets) are surfaced by diamond_sapphire_ticket_pac_anomaly, and the single-event TargetDomainName markers by forged_ticket_domain_field_anomaly.
falsepositives: Legacy RC4-only service accounts (this rule will fire daily until they are remediated)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17') AND (NOT COALESCE((ServiceName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName='krbtgt'), 0)))
title: Golden Ticket Hunting Trigger (RC4 TGS for User Service)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for step 1 of the ESC8 relay chain (adcs_esc8_web_enrollment_relay.yml). Matches a remote 5145 access over IPC$ on a Domain Controller to a named pipe that exposes a coercible RPC interface, narrowed so that routine domain member traffic does not satisfy it. Pipes with little legitimate remote client traffic to a DC match on their own: efsrpc (MS-EFSR, PetitPotam), netdfs (MS-DFSNM, DFSCoerce), FssagentRpc (MS-FSRVP, ShadowCoerce) and spoolss (MS-RPRN, the printer bug). The MS-EFSR alternate pipes that members open all day (lsarpc, lsass, samr, netlogon) match only with AccessMask 0x3, the access the Impacket SMB client requests; PetitPotam.py uses lsarpc by default. It covers, for this chain only, pipes that coercion_relay/petitpotam_efsrpc_coercion.yml and coercion_relay/coercion_multi_vector_named_pipes.yml alert on, scoped to the DCs whose machine accounts the chain's other steps look for.
falsepositives: DFS management (netdfs), VSS for SMB file shares backup (FssagentRpc) or a DC that is also a print server (spoolss)
Python or Impacket-based administration tooling that opens lsarpc or samr on a DC (it requests the same 0x3 mask)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND ShareName LIKE '%\\IPC$' ESCAPE '\' AND (Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\')) AND ((RelativeTargetName='efsrpc' OR RelativeTargetName='netdfs' OR RelativeTargetName='FssagentRpc' OR RelativeTargetName='spoolss') OR ((RelativeTargetName='lsarpc' OR RelativeTargetName='lsass' OR RelativeTargetName='samr' OR RelativeTargetName='netlogon') AND AccessMask='0x3')) AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1' OR IpAddress='::ffff:127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='-'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Coercion Named Pipe Opened on a Domain Controller (ESC8 Chain Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting record for one single-event marker of a forged Kerberos ticket. The account domain in a forged ticket's PAC is whatever the forging tool was given, and older Mimikatz builds wrote a blank domain. This rule flags a Kerberos network logon (4624 LogonType 3) whose TargetDomainName is blank. Microsoft's 4624 page lists the NetBIOS name, the lower-case FQDN and the upper-case FQDN as ordinary renderings of the account domain ("Formats vary"), and its 4769 page says the realm "can appear in a variety of formats" and "can be empty in some cases", so an FQDN on 4624 and a blank or lower-case realm on 4769 are not used as markers. The branch fires on member servers for Silver Tickets and on any host for Golden Tickets.
falsepositives: Unknown. Microsoft's 4624 page does not list a blank New Logon account domain as a normal rendering, but no baseline of Kerberos network logons was taken for this release
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND AuthenticationPackageName='Kerberos') AND (TargetDomainName='' OR TargetDomainName='-'))
title: Forged Kerberos Ticket Domain Field Anomaly (Golden or Silver Ticket Marker)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting trigger for constrained / resource-based constrained delegation exploitation. Rubeus s4u and Impacket getST perform S4U2self then S4U2proxy, producing 4769 service-ticket requests carrying a Transited Services attribute (the impersonated path). Anomalous combinations of impersonated user plus target SPN are the abuse signal. PDF reference: "Constrained delegation / Resource-Based Constrained Delegation".
falsepositives: Legitimate constrained-delegation applications (IIS to SQL, etc). Baseline the expected impersonation paths and exclude them.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4769 AND TransmittedServices LIKE '%@%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Kerberos S4U2Proxy Delegation Abuse (Transited Services)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for correlations. A successful Kerberos authentication service request (4768 with Status 0x0). Used by the noPac chain correlation to find a TGT requested for the spoofed name a computer account was renamed to. Not an alert on its own; volume equals the number of interactive and service logons in the domain.
falsepositives: Every successful logon. Base rule only.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4768 AND Status='0x0')
title: Kerberos TGT Issued (Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for step 3 of the ESC8 relay chain (adcs_esc8_web_enrollment_relay.yml). Matches CA events 4886 (request received) and 4887 (certificate issued) whose Requester is a Domain Controller machine account. DCs enrol for their own certificates routinely, so this is informational on its own; it becomes the ESC8 signal when it follows a coercion and an NTLM logon by the same DC on the CA host.
falsepositives: Domain Controller auto-enrolment for DomainController, DomainControllerAuthentication and KerberosAuthentication templates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4886 OR EventID=4887) AND (Requester LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR Requester LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Certificate Request or Issuance with a Domain Controller as Requester (Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Records the trust password reset sequence that Microsoft attributes to the automatic trust password rotation: 4716 (trusted domain information modified) followed by 4724 and/or 4742 on the trust account, all with ANONYMOUS LOGON (S-1-5-7, logon ID 0x3E6) as the subject. The rotation runs every 30 days per trust, so this is a hunting record, not an alert. Its value is the cadence. A reset outside the expected interval for a trust, or several in a short time, can be a Zerologon-style reset of the trust account over Netlogon, which carries the same anonymous subject.
falsepositives: The automatic trust password rotation itself, once per trust roughly every 30 days. Base record only.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-7' AND SubjectLogonId='0x3e6') AND (EventID=4716 OR ((EventID=4724 OR EventID=4742) AND TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TRUST\_ACCOUNT$' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Trust Account Password Reset by ANONYMOUS LOGON (Automatic Rotation or Netlogon Abuse)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Records Volume Shadow Copy service Application log event 8224 on a Domain Controller ("The VSS service is shutting down due to idle timeout"). The service starts on demand and stops after a quiet period, so 8224 marks the end of a VSS session: something created, listed or deleted shadow copies shortly before. On a DC that has no scheduled backup in that window, it is a pivot to look for vssadmin, diskshadow, wmic shadowcopy or ntdsutil snapshot activity, including when process telemetry is missing.
falsepositives: Every scheduled or manual backup, System Restore and any other VSS requester; this is a hunting pivot, not an alert
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name='VSS' AND EventID=8224)
title: VSS Service Idle Shutdown After Use (8224)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Weekly hygiene hunt. 4780 is logged on the PDC emulator when SDProp, which runs every hour, finds that the ACL of an account in a protected group (adminCount 1) differs from the ACL of AdminSDHolder and resets it. Each hit names an account whose ACL was changed since the last run, or a new member of a protected group. Review the list for accounts that should not be protected, and for repeated resets of one account, which point to a tool or person rewriting its ACL.
falsepositives: Every legitimate protected-group addition and every delegated ACL change on an admin account produces one event at the next SDProp run
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4780
title: SDProp Reset the ACL of a Protected Account (4780 Hygiene Hunt)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Base rule for the Shadow Credentials use-step correlation. A successful 4768 with a PKINIT pre-authentication type (15, 16 or 17; certificate or key-trust authentication) and a populated CertIssuerName. Smart card, certificate and Windows Hello for Business logons all produce it; not an alert on its own.
falsepositives: Every smart card, certificate and WHfB logon. Base rule only.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 AND (PreAuthType=15 OR PreAuthType=16 OR PreAuthType=17) AND Status='0x0' AND CertIssuerName IS NOT NULL) AND (NOT COALESCE((CertIssuerName='' OR CertIssuerName='-'), 0)))
title: Kerberos PKINIT TGT Issued With Certificate (Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting rule. Records a referral ticket for a trust (4769 whose ServiceName is the trust account) that this DC issued with RC4 (0x17). In an AES-only forest an RC4 referral points at a client or a trust forced down to RC4, which is the cipher Mimikatz trust tickets use by default with a dumped trust key. It does not detect a forged trust ticket. A forged referral is minted offline by the attacker and presented to the DC of the other realm, so the DC that would have issued it logs nothing, and the 4769 on the target DC describes the service ticket it issues, not the referral it was given. The companion rules cover the verifiable trust signals. trust_account_password_reset flags a trust key set by a named account and trust_ticket_foreign_account_domain flags a ticket for an unknown realm.
falsepositives: Legacy trusts and clients that still negotiate RC4 (populate filter_known_trust_principals)
Misconfigured cross-realm clients
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 AND Status='0x0' AND ServiceName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TRUST\_ACCOUNT$' ESCAPE '\' AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17') AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_TRUST\_USER%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: RC4 Inter-Realm Referral Ticket Issued Over a Trust (Hunt)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Informational base rule for the AD CS rule family. Matches every Certificate Services request (4886), issuance (4887) and template load (4898) recorded by the issuing CA. It fires on every certificate the CA handles, including routine auto-enrolment, so it never enters the alert queue on its own. Use it as the hunting stream and as the event set the specific AD CS rules narrow: adcs_san_upn_anomaly.yml (SAN supplied as a request attribute, ESC6), adcs_esc3_enrollment_agent_request.yml (enrollment-agent template, ESC3), adcs_cert_request_dc_requester_base.yml and the ESC8 chain in adcs_esc8_web_enrollment_relay.yml. Tooling indicators (Certify, Certipy) live in adcs_tooling_process.yml because they are process_creation events.
falsepositives: Every legitimate enrolment and auto-enrolment. This is a base rule and is expected to match routine traffic.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4886 OR EventID=4887 OR EventID=4898)
title: AD CS Certificate Request, Issuance or Template Load (Base)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunt for the client side of Configuration Manager Run Scripts and CMPivot: CcmExec.exe starts PowerShell on a script from C:\Windows\CCM\ScriptStore. This is what an operator who has taken over the site, or a SharpSCCM user with Run Scripts rights, makes every targeted client do, but it is also what every legitimate Run Scripts or CMPivot run makes every targeted client do, so it fires once per client per run. It was the third branch of sccm_cmpivot_abuse.yml until v4.0.0 and was split out as a hunt.
falsepositives: Every legitimate Run Scripts or CMPivot run, once on each targeted client. The client process runs as SYSTEM and the event names neither the operator nor the console, so it cannot be baselined by operator on the client side. Attribute it at the site server (Run Scripts approval and script status messages) and alert only on runs that are not approved there.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (ParentImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\CCM\\CcmExec.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\CCM\\ScriptStore\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: SCCM Client Runs a Run Scripts or CMPivot Script from the ScriptStore (Hunt)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting trigger for AzureHound-style cloud enumeration: a high volume of outbound connections to graph.microsoft.com from a single on-prem host running PowerShell, dotnet or an unsigned binary. Requires Sysmon EID 22 (DNS) or EID 3 (network) with process attribution.
falsepositives: Intune/Entra management tooling and Office apps (baseline per host; this is hunt-queue)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=22 AND (QueryName LIKE '%graph.microsoft.com%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE(((Image LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\MsSense.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Common Files\\microsoft shared\\ClickToRun\\OfficeClickToRun.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (Image LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Azure Advanced Threat Protection Sensor\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND Image LIKE '%\\Microsoft.Tri.Sensor.exe' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Microsoft Graph API Enumeration Candidate Host

author: 404secnotfound
description: Hunting trigger for Diamond and Sapphire tickets, the AES-based evasion of RC4 Golden Ticket detection. The signal is a 4769 service-ticket request using AES where no 4768 TGT was issued for the same user within the preceding hours. Implement the absence check as a SIEM correlation; this rule surfaces the AES TGS candidates.
falsepositives: Normal AES Kerberos activity. This is hunt-queue only; the fidelity comes from correlating against missing 4768 TGT issuance.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 AND (TicketEncryptionType='0x12' OR TicketEncryptionType='0x13')) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Diamond / Sapphire Ticket Hunting (AES TGS Without Preceding TGT)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the victim side of LLMNR poisoning. A Windows host that fails to resolve a name in DNS multicasts an LLMNR query to 224.0.0.252 or ff02::1:3 on UDP 5355 from an ephemeral port, and a poisoner (Responder, Inveigh) answers by unicast from its UDP 5355 to that ephemeral port. Sysmon on the victim records the answer as an inbound UDP flow with SourcePort 5355 and a DestinationPort that is not 5355. Peer queries from other hosts arrive on DestinationPort 5355 and are excluded. In a domain where DNS resolves every legitimate name, LLMNR answers should be rare, and an answer from a host that is not the name's owner is the poisoning footprint. This rule needs no Sysmon on the attacker's machine, which is usually a Linux box.
falsepositives: Legitimate LLMNR answers from the real owner of a name that DNS does not resolve (non-domain devices, lab machines); LLMNR is peer-to-peer, so the real owner answers, not the DNS server
Networks where LLMNR is still widely relied on; disable LLMNR by GPO, after which any hit is suspicious
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Initiated='false' AND Protocol='udp' AND SourcePort=5355) AND (NOT COALESCE((DestinationPort=5355 OR (SourceIp='127.0.0.1' OR SourceIp='::1') OR SourceIp LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_LLMNR\_RESPONDER\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: LLMNR Response Received by a Workstation (Victim-Side Poisoning Signal)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects NTLM relay of a coerced Domain Controller account to a member server, seen from the DC that validates it. NTLM Operational event 8004 is written on the DC for each NTLM authentication it validates and names the user, the client-claimed workstation and the secure channel name, which is the server that received the authentication. When PetitPotam, the printer bug or DFSCoerce makes DC01 authenticate to an attacker and the attacker relays it to a member server (an AD CS web enrollment host for ESC8, an SMB server, an SCCM site server), the DC logs 8004 with user DC01$ and a secure channel name that is the relay target. Domain Controllers rarely use NTLM against member servers, so a DC account arriving through a non-DC secure channel is the relay shape. This covers relays to member servers that the 4624 rules only see if the member server forwards its Security log.
falsepositives: A Domain Controller that reaches a member server share or web service by IP address or by an alias without an SPN, so NTLM is used instead of Kerberos (fix the name or SPN, or add a narrow filter on that SChannelName)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational' AND ((EventID=8004 AND (UserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR UserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((SChannelName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_NAME' ESCAPE '\' OR SChannelName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_NAME' ESCAPE '\') OR (SChannelName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_NAME.%' ESCAPE '\' OR SChannelName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_NAME.%' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: Domain Controller Account NTLM Authentication Through a Non-DC Server (NTLM 8004)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects cmd.exe or PowerShell started by WmiPrvSE.exe under a logon session other than SYSTEM, LOCAL SERVICE or NETWORK SERVICE. Remote Win32_Process.Create (wmiexec with -nooutput, wmic /node, Invoke-WmiMethod -ComputerName) runs the child in the calling user's logon session, while most management agents that use WMI locally run as SYSTEM.
falsepositives: Administrators running remote commands through WMI by hand
Software deployment and monitoring tools that call Win32_Process.Create remotely with a named account
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((ParentImage LIKE '%\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((LogonId='0x3e7' OR LogonId='0x3e4' OR LogonId='0x3e5'), 0))))
title: WmiPrvSE Spawned cmd.exe or PowerShell in a User Context

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a successful service ticket request (4769, Status 0x0) where the requesting account's realm (TargetDomainName) is neither the local domain nor a domain on the trusted-domain list. A golden or trust ticket forged with a made-up, mistyped or non-trusted realm string shows a realm the DC has no business seeing. A forged trust ticket that carries the real realm of a trusted domain is filtered by design and is not visible to this rule; see the note of trust_ticket_forging for the native test that covers it.
falsepositives: Domains not yet listed in filter_known_domains (child domains of this forest, every domain of a trusted forest), or a listed domain whose DNS or NetBIOS form is missing, since Microsoft documents that Account Domain can appear as CONTOSO, contoso.local or CONTOSO.LOCAL
MIT or other non-Windows realms with a configured realm trust
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 AND Status='0x0') AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetDomainName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetDomainName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN\_NETBIOS' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetDomainName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TRUSTED\_DOMAIN' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetDomainName='' OR TargetDomainName='-')), 0)))
title: Service Ticket Issued for Account From Unknown Realm

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DNS SRV queries used to locate Domain Controllers, the PDC emulator, site-specific Domain Controllers, Global Catalogs and Kerberos services from a process other than the Windows DC locator. Requires Sysmon EID 22 (DNS query), which records lookups made through the Windows DNS Client API, for example Resolve-DnsName, .NET Dns calls and tools that call DnsQuery directly. PDF reference: "nslookup -type=SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.<DOMAIN>".
falsepositives: Admin tooling (ADUC via mmc.exe, PowerShell AD module) on jump hosts
Line-of-business applications that locate a Domain Controller through DnsQuery instead of DsGetDcName
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=22 AND ((QueryName LIKE '%\_ldap.\_tcp.dc.\_msdcs%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%\_ldap.\_tcp.pdc.\_msdcs%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%\_ldap.\_tcp.gc.\_msdcs%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%.\_sites.dc.\_msdcs%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%\_kerberos.\_tcp.dc.\_msdcs%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%\_gc.\_tcp%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%\_kpasswd.\_tcp%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\dns.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image='System'), 0))))
title: DNS SRV Record Query for Active Directory Discovery

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DNS Server event 6004 in the DNS Server event log, which the pack maps to a refused zone transfer request (a request for a zone the server does not hold or is not authoritative for). A recon signal only. The sibling dns_zone_transfer_analytic reads the verified analytic channel events 270 and 266 and should be preferred where analytic logging is on.
falsepositives: Misconfigured secondaries or stub zones requesting a zone this server no longer hosts (allowlist the source address in the SIEM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='DNS Server' AND EventID=6004
title: DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR/IXFR) Attempt via DNS Server Event Log

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the victim side of mitm6. Windows prefers IPv6 and sends DHCPv6 Solicit messages even on IPv4-only networks; mitm6 answers them from UDP 547 (the DHCPv6 server and relay port) to the client's UDP 546, hands out a link-local address and names itself as the IPv6 DNS server, then answers WPAD and other lookups. Sysmon on the victim records the answer as an inbound UDP flow with SourcePort 547 and DestinationPort 546. In a network with no DHCPv6 service any such flow is a rogue server; where DHCPv6 is deployed, only the sanctioned servers and relay agents should appear. Replaces mitm6_ipv6_dhcpv6_poisoning, whose event IDs were DHCPv4 client service start and stop events.
falsepositives: Sanctioned DHCPv6 servers or router relay agents not yet listed in filter_sanctioned_dhcpv6 (relay agents answer from their own link-local address on each segment)
Newly deployed IPv6 or DHCPv6 infrastructure
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Initiated='false' AND Protocol='udp' AND SourcePort=547 AND DestinationPort=546) AND (NOT COALESCE((SourceIp LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DHCPV6\_SERVER\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: DHCPv6 Reply from an Unexpected Server (mitm6 Rogue DHCPv6)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Windows host successfully resolving wpad or isatap, bare or under a domain suffix. Windows DNS servers refuse these names by default (the DNS global query block list contains WPAD and ISATAP), so in a domain that does not publish WPAD the lookup the browser and WinHTTP make for proxy auto-discovery ends in name error. It completes with an address when something else answers it: mitm6, after its rogue DHCPv6 reply has made the attacker the host's IPv6 DNS server; Responder or Inveigh answering the LLMNR or NBT-NS fallback for wpad; or a wpad record in AD-integrated DNS (ADIDNS spoofing) after the block list was changed or side-stepped. Each is the step that points the host's proxy auto-configuration, and so its HTTP NTLM authentication, at the attacker.
falsepositives: Environments that publish WPAD or ISATAP on purpose and removed them from the global query block list (populate filter_sanctioned_wpad with the proxy auto-config host)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-DNS Client Events/Operational' AND ((EventID=3008 AND QueryStatus=0) AND ((QueryName='wpad' OR QueryName='isatap') OR (QueryName LIKE 'wpad.%' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE 'isatap.%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((QueryResults LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_WPAD\_SERVER\_IP;%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: WPAD or ISATAP Name Resolved Successfully (mitm6 or Poisoner DNS Injection)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Trigger rule for the use step of a forged or misissued certificate. Matches a successful 4768 TGT request authenticated with PKINIT (PreAuthType 15, 16 or 17) that carries certificate details. The abuse signal is that the account the certificate was issued to (the Requester on the issuing 4887) differs from the account the TGT was issued for (TargetUserName), which is what ESC1, ESC6, ESC8 and Certifried certificates look like when used. 4768 does not carry the certificate SAN, so the comparison has to be done by joining on the certificate serial number or thumbprint; see the note.
falsepositives: Every legitimate smart card, Windows Hello for Business certificate trust and device certificate logon. In estates that use them widely this rule is volume until the native join below is in place.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 AND Status='0x0' AND (PreAuthType=15 OR PreAuthType=16 OR PreAuthType=17)) AND (NOT COALESCE((CertIssuerName='' OR CertIssuerName='-'), 0)))
title: PKINIT TGT Request Candidate for Certificate SAN and Account Mismatch

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects reads of the local administrator password stored by LAPS. The 4662 Properties field records the schemaIDGUID of each attribute read, not the attribute name, so the legacy ms-Mcs-AdmPwd attribute (a schema extension whose GUID is generated per forest) must be supplied as a placeholder. Windows LAPS attributes are part of the base schema and carry fixed GUIDs; populate them from your schema with the command in the note until they are confirmed in this pack. Bulk reads by one principal (Get-LAPSPasswords, LAPSToolkit, bloodhound LAPS collection) are the abuse pattern. PDF reference: "Get-LAPSPasswords -DomainController <ip_dc>".
falsepositives: Authorised LAPS administrators and help-desk tooling (populate filter_authorised_readers)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND AccessMask='0x10' AND (Properties LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_LAPS\_ADMPWD\_SCHEMA\_GUID%' ESCAPE '\' OR Properties LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_WINDOWS\_LAPS\_PASSWORD\_GUID%' ESCAPE '\' OR Properties LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_WINDOWS\_LAPS\_ENCRYPTEDPASSWORD\_GUID%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_LAPS\_READER\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: LAPS Password Attribute Read (Legacy LAPS and Windows LAPS)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects anonymous (null) SMB logon attempts on a Domain Controller or member server. Mirrors tradecraft from enum4linux, smbmap, smbclient, CrackMapExec and nmap smb-vuln scripts run with empty or guest credentials to enumerate shares, users and policies before any creds are held.
falsepositives: Legacy applications that intentionally use null sessions (rare on modern AD)
Vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7) authenticating with null
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND AuthenticationPackageName='NTLM') AND ((TargetUserName='ANONYMOUS LOGON' OR TargetUserName='Guest') OR (TargetDomainName='NT AUTHORITY' OR TargetDomainName='ANONYMOUS LOGON' OR TargetDomainName='')) AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress='-' OR IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1'), 0)))
title: SMB Null or Anonymous Session Enumeration Against Domain Controller

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write (5136) to any attribute of CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System other than nTSecurityDescriptor. AdminSDHolder is the template whose ACL SDProp copies to every protected account every hour, and nothing in normal operation writes to it. DACL and owner changes on it (the classic AdminSDHolder backdoor) are covered at critical by acl_dacl_abuse/dacl_modification_privileged_object; this rule catches the remaining writes, which indicate hands-on tampering with the object or tooling testing write access to it, without alerting twice on a DACL edit.
falsepositives: Directory migration or backup-restore tools that rewrite system objects (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND ObjectDN LIKE 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor'), 0)))
title: AdminSDHolder Object Attribute Modified (Non-DACL Attribute)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects an account password reset performed against another user via 4724 ("An attempt was made to reset an account's password"). This is the abuse path for accounts granted the ForceChangePassword extended right through ACL abuse. Self-service resets (Subject equals Target) should be filtered in the SIEM enrichment layer because Sigma cannot compare two fields directly. PDF reference: "ForceChangePassword".
falsepositives: Help-desk password reset workflows (correlate with ticketing)
Self-service password resets (filter where SubjectUserName equals TargetUserName in SIEM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4724 AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: User Password Reset by Administrator or Delegated Right (Force Change Password)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects removal of the Microsoft Defender attack surface reduction rule "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem" (GUID 9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2) from the registry: the value named after the rule GUID is deleted, or the whole ASR Rules key that holds it is deleted. Remove-MpPreference, and Set-MpPreference with a rule list that leaves the GUID out, take the rule off the host without writing an Off value, which the registry_set sibling cannot see.
falsepositives: A Group Policy object that configured the rule being unlinked or edited, which makes the Group Policy client delete the policy value on many hosts at once (check the GPO change history)
Planned ASR roll-back by endpoint administrators (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND ((EventID=12 AND (EventType='DeleteKey' OR EventType='DeleteValue')) AND ((EventType='DeleteValue' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\\ASR\\Rules\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2' ESCAPE '\') OR (EventType='DeleteKey' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\\ASR\\Rules' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Defender ASR Rule Block Credential Stealing from LSASS Removed (Registry Delete)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects SMB-signing enumeration tools started on a Windows host: the nmap smb-security-mode and smb2-security-mode scripts, NetExec or CrackMapExec in SMB mode (with or without --gen-relay-list), and Responder's RunFinger. Finding hosts that do not require SMB signing is the step that builds an ntlmrelayx target list. This is a tool-only rule. It fires only when the scanner runs on a Windows host that logs process creation; a scan from a Linux attacker box is invisible to it. PDF reference: "nmap -Pn -sS -T4 --open --script smb-security-mode -p445".
falsepositives: Internal vulnerability scans and audit tooling run from Windows scanner hosts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%smb-security-mode%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%smb2-security-mode%' ESCAPE '\') OR CommandLine LIKE '%--gen-relay-list%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%RunFinger.py%' ESCAPE '\' OR (((Image LIKE '%\\nxc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\netexec.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\cme.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\crackmapexec.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%\\nxc.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\cme.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%netexec%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%crackmapexec%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% nxc %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% cme %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\nxc %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\cme %' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE 'nxc %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE 'cme %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE 'nxc.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE 'cme.exe%' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '% smb %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Recon Scan for SMB Signing Not Required (Tool Execution on Windows)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center events 39 and 40 in the System log of a Domain Controller. Event 39 means a valid certificate could not be mapped to the account in a strong way (no SID extension, no explicit or key-trust mapping); event 40 means the certificate was issued before the account existed and no strong mapping was found. Forged or attacker-requested certificates from templates that omit the SID extension (ESC9, ESC10, CT_FLAG_NO_SECURITY_EXTENSION) or from an offline or rogue CA land here, as do legacy certificates that predate the May 2022 update.
falsepositives: Smart card and device certificates issued before the KB5014754 SID extension was added, or issued by third-party CAs without explicit altSecurityIdentities mapping. Expect volume until those certificates are reissued or mapped.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center' OR Provider_Name='Kdcsvc') AND (EventID=39 OR EventID=40))
title: KDC Certificate Without Strong Mapping or Predating the Account (KB5014754 Events 39, 40)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects addition of a member to the Builtin Administrators group (S-1-5-32-544) or Builtin Remote Desktop Users (S-1-5-32-555) through 4732. On a domain controller these are the domain's builtin groups, and Administrators there is equivalent to Domain Admins. Member servers and workstations log the same event for their local groups, which is routine administration, so this rule is split from domain_admin_group_addition at a lower level. Matched by SID and by English name so localised group names still match.
falsepositives: Local administrator and remote-access grants on member servers and workstations by help desk or deployment tooling
Tier-0 admin onboarding on DCs (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4732 AND ((TargetSid='S-1-5-32-544' OR TargetSid='S-1-5-32-555') OR (TargetUserName='Administrators' OR TargetUserName='Remote Desktop Users')))
title: Member Added to Builtin Administrators or Remote Desktop Users

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a null (anonymous) SMB session opening one of the RPC named pipes used to enumerate a domain without credentials: srvsvc (shares and sessions), samr (users and groups), lsarpc (policy and SID lookups, the pipe lookupsid.py and rpcclient lookupsids use for RID cycling) and wkssvc (workstation and logged-on users). 5145 with SubjectUserName ANONYMOUS LOGON on share \\*\IPC$ is the share-level corroboration of the anonymous network logon caught by smb_null_anonymous_session_enumeration, and it names the interface the tool reached. Mirrors enum4linux, rpcclient -U "" -N, CrackMapExec and smbclient null-session enumeration.
falsepositives: Legacy NAS appliances, printers and pre-Windows 2000 clients that still resolve names over anonymous lsarpc
Vulnerability scanners running unauthenticated SMB checks
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND ShareName LIKE '%\\IPC$' ESCAPE '\' AND SubjectUserName='ANONYMOUS LOGON' AND (RelativeTargetName='srvsvc' OR RelativeTargetName='samr' OR RelativeTargetName='lsarpc' OR RelativeTargetName='wkssvc')) AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1'), 0)))
title: Anonymous Access to Enumeration Named Pipes over IPC$

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a detailed file share access (5145) to the winreg named pipe on IPC$ from a source address that is not an allowlisted management or scanning host. Remote secretsdump, CrackMapExec --sam/--lsa and reg.exe save against a remote host all open winreg to save the SAM, SECURITY and SYSTEM hives through the Remote Registry service.
falsepositives: Vulnerability scanners, SCCM and monitoring servers that read the registry remotely (add their addresses to filter_management_hosts)
Administrators running regedit "Connect Network Registry" from their workstation
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND ShareName LIKE '%\\IPC$' ESCAPE '\' AND RelativeTargetName='winreg') AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_REMOTE\_REGISTRY\_MGMT\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_REMOTE\_REGISTRY\_MGMT\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1'), 0)))
title: Remote Registry winreg Pipe Opened from a Non-Management Host

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects MS14-068 / goldenPac PAC forgery against a domain controller. The tool asks for a TGT without a PAC, then presents a forged PAC in a TGS request for krbtgt. In the JPCERT/CC lab analysis of the exploit the DC logged 4769 for ServiceName krbtgt with failure code 0x3C (KRB_ERR_GENERIC) during the exploitation. PDF reference: "goldenPac.py -dc-ip <dc_ip> <domain>/<user>:'<pwd>'@<target>".
falsepositives: KRB_ERR_GENERIC for krbtgt from token bloat (group membership that overloads the PAC) or from password changes that have not replicated (MS Learn 4769 failure table); baseline per account before routing
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4769 AND ServiceName='krbtgt' AND Status='0x3c')
title: MS14-068 GoldenPAC PAC Forgery Indicators

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a successful PKINIT TGT request (4768 PreAuthType 15, 16 or 17) whose certificate issuer is not on the allowlist of enterprise CA issuer names. Shadow Credentials tooling (Whisker, pyWhisker, Certipy shadow) authenticates with a self-signed key-trust certificate it generated, so the issuer is an arbitrary name rather than the enterprise CA. A forged certificate from a stolen non-enterprise CA key also lands here.
falsepositives: Windows Hello for Business key trust, which also authenticates with a self-signed key-trust certificate, so the issuer can differ per user and cannot be baselined as a short issuer list. In WHfB key-trust estates, scope the rule by account population in the native query (exclude members of the WHfB deployment group by lookup) or deploy it only for accounts outside WHfB scope, such as Tier-0 and service accounts.
Additional enterprise or partner CAs not yet listed in filter_enterprise_ca
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 AND (PreAuthType=15 OR PreAuthType=16 OR PreAuthType=17) AND Status='0x0' AND CertIssuerName IS NOT NULL) AND (NOT COALESCE(((CertIssuerName='' OR CertIssuerName='-') OR CertIssuerName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_ENTERPRISE\_CA\_ISSUER' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Kerberos PKINIT Logon With Certificate Not Issued by the Enterprise CA

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the CA-side record of a certificate template change. The CA logs 4899 (a Certificate Services template was updated) and 4900 (Certificate Services template security was updated) when it loads a template whose content or security descriptor changed since it last loaded it. ESC4 abuse rewrites a template's flags, EKUs or DACL, enrols, and often reverts; the CA records the old and new content even when the directory-side 5136 SACL (adcs_template_acl_modification.yml) is missing.
falsepositives: Planned template changes by PKI administrators (rare, ticketed). The event does not name who changed the template; join to 5136 on the template object for the actor.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4899 OR EventID=4900)
title: Certificate Template Content or Security Updated as Seen by the CA (4899, 4900)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the Microsoft Defender attack surface reduction rule "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem" (GUID 9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2) being set to Off (0), Audit (2) or Not configured (5) in the registry, in either the local Defender configuration key written by Set-MpPreference or the Group Policy key. On hosts where LSA protection and Credential Guard cannot be enabled this rule is the remaining LSASS guard, so switching it off precedes a credential dump.
falsepositives: A staged ASR roll-out that puts the rule in Audit mode on a pilot group (ticketed; the writes come from the Group Policy client or the MDM agent on many hosts at once)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\\ASR\\Rules\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2' ESCAPE '\') AND (Details=0 OR Details=2 OR Details=5 OR Details='DWORD (0x00000000)' OR Details='DWORD (0x00000002)' OR Details='DWORD (0x00000005)')))
title: Defender ASR Rule Block Credential Stealing from LSASS Turned Off (Registry)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write to msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes (5136 Value Added) on the krbtgt account, an RODC krbtgt_<number> account, or a computer object in the Domain Controllers OU. Re-enabling RC4 or DES on these objects is encryption downgrade persistence: it keeps RC4 tickets (forgeable with an NT hash, and required by Skeleton Key) working after a hardening project disabled them. The attribute holds a decimal bit mask (0x4 RC4, 0x8 AES128, 0x10 AES256), shown in AttributeValue. DCs write their own value when the Kerberos encryption-type policy applies, so DC-object writes by the DC machine accounts in the allowlist are excluded; writes on krbtgt are never excluded.
falsepositives: Kerberos hardening projects that set AES-only values (for example 24) on krbtgt or DCs; ticketed, and the value shows the direction of the change
Entra Kerberos key rotation touching CN=krbtgt_AzureAD
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes' AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\') AND ((ObjectDN LIKE 'CN=krbtgt,%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectDN LIKE 'CN=krbtgt\_%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ObjectDN LIKE '%,OU=Domain Controllers,%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: Kerberos Encryption Types Changed on krbtgt or Domain Controller Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Netlogon events 5827 and 5828 (vulnerable secure channel from a machine or trust account denied by an enforcing DC) and 5830 and 5831 (vulnerable connection allowed because the account is on the "Domain controller: Allow vulnerable Netlogon secure channel connections" policy). Denied events mean a client attempted the vulnerable handshake and was stopped, which is either an unpatched legacy device or an exploitation attempt that failed. Allowed-by-policy events are a standing exposure to review. Split from the Zerologon rule so that 5829 (allowed, exploitable) can page on its own.
falsepositives: Legacy non-Windows devices (NAS, printers, Samba) using the vulnerable Netlogon handshake (inventory and remediate; exclude by SamAccountName once confirmed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((EventID=5827 OR EventID=5828) OR (EventID=5830 OR EventID=5831))
title: Vulnerable Netlogon Secure Channel Denied or Allowed by Policy (Zerologon Inventory)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4662 directory access to a KDS root key object (msKds-ProvRootKey, under CN=Master Root Keys,CN=Group Key Distribution Service,CN=Services,CN=Configuration) or a read of its msKds-RootKeyData attribute by any principal that is not an allowlisted Domain Controller. GoldenGMSA and Golden dMSA read the root key once and can then compute the password of every gMSA or dMSA in the forest offline, indefinitely. Only the Key Distribution Service on the DCs reads these objects in normal operation.
falsepositives: Domain or enterprise admins creating a KDS root key (Add-KdsRootKey) or inspecting it in ADSI Edit; rare and ticketed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4662 AND ((ObjectType LIKE '%aa02fd41-17e0-4f18-8687-b2239649736b%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectType LIKE '%msKds-ProvRootKey%' ESCAPE '\') OR Properties LIKE '%26627c27-08a2-0a40-a1b1-8dce85b42993%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: KDS Root Key Read by Non-DC Principal (GoldenGMSA)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects abuse of Configuration Manager (SCCM / MECM) for discovery, credential theft and lateral movement. Two branches. (1) SharpSCCM by image name, PE original file name or its name in the command line; its verbs (local secrets, get naa, exec, invoke client-push) recover Network Access Account (NAA) credentials or push commands through the site. (2) ConfigMgr PowerShell cmdlets that list, create or run scripts and CMPivot queries against collections (Get-CMScript, New-CMScript, Invoke-CMScript, Approve-CMScript, Invoke-CMPivot). The client side of Run Scripts and CMPivot (CcmExec.exe starting PowerShell on a ScriptStore script) is the hunt sccm_run_scripts_client_execution.yml. PDF reference: "sccm CMPivot".
falsepositives: Sanctioned SCCM operators running the ConfigMgr cmdlets from the console or an admin host (baseline the User and the host; this branch runs as the operator, so both are in the event)
Authorised red-team use of SharpSCCM
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\SharpSCCM.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='SharpSCCM.exe') OR CommandLine LIKE '%SharpSCCM%' ESCAPE '\' OR ((Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Get-CMScript%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%New-CMScript%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-CMScript%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Approve-CMScript%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-CMPivot%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: SCCM CMPivot, Run Scripts and SharpSCCM Abuse

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects 4662 events in which a principal that is not an allowlisted Domain Controller exercises only the DS-Replication-Get-Changes-In-Filtered-Set control access right (89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c), without Get-Changes or Get-Changes-All on the same event. Those two are the critical DCSync rule's signal. A filtered-set-only event is either partial replication tooling or one half of a DCSync whose other events are logged separately, so it is kept at medium to avoid a second critical alert for the same activity.
falsepositives: Writable DC replication partners missing from the allowlist, including Global Catalogs and DCs of other domains in the forest
Directory synchronisation products that request the filtered set
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND AccessMask='0x100' AND Properties LIKE '%89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((Properties LIKE '%1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2%' ESCAPE '\' OR Properties LIKE '%1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2%' ESCAPE '\') OR (SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_MSOL\_OR\_ADSYNC\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: Replication In Filtered Set Right Exercised by Non-DC (Partial DCSync)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Mimikatz / Pypykatz / Kekeo command-line strings. This rule catches only operators with poor opsec (no obfuscation). For higher-fidelity coverage see the Sysmon-enriched sibling rules: mimikatz_dll_image_load_lsass.yml and lsass_process_access_credential_dump.yml. PDF reference: "mimikatz 'privilege::debug' 'sekurlsa::logonPasswords'".
falsepositives: Authorised red team activity tracked through ticketing
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::logonpasswords%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::tickets%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::minidump%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::pth%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::ekeys%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sekurlsa::dpapi%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::dcsync%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::sam%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::lsa%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::secrets%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::cache%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::trust%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::backupkeys%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::setntlm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::changentlm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::golden%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::ptt%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::ptc%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::list /export%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::purge%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sid::patch%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sid::add%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%event::drop%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%misc::addsid%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%crypto::capi%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%crypto::cng%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%misc::skeleton%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%misc::memssp%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%privilege::debug%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%token::elevate%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%!processprotect%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%pypykatz %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-Mimikatz%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString%' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='mimikatz.exe' OR OriginalFileName='mimilib.dll' OR OriginalFileName='mimidrv.sys')))
title: Mimikatz Command Line Indicators (Low-Opsec Operator)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects adminCount being written with the value 1 (5136 Value Added) by a principal that is not a domain controller. adminCount is set by SDProp, which runs on the PDC emulator as SYSTEM, when an object becomes a member of a protected group. A manual write marks a non-protected object as protected without group membership (the "SDProp bypass" persistence named in the plan). [Inference] The aim is to make a backdoor account look like a former administrator to reviewers and to clean-up tooling that keys on adminCount, usually together with a custom ACL and disabled inheritance on the object.
falsepositives: Identity management or migration tools (ADMT, some IAM connectors) that copy adminCount between objects
Administrators re-stamping adminCount by hand during a protected-account clean-up
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='adminCount' AND AttributeValue=1 AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: adminCount Set to 1 by a Principal Other Than SDProp

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DNS Server audit event 515 (record created) or 519 (record created via dynamic update) for a record whose name is wpad, isatap or the wildcard *. These names let an attacker answer proxy auto-discovery, ISATAP tunnelling or every non-existent name inside the domain (ADIDNS poisoning with Powermad Invoke-DNSUpdate, Inveigh or dnstool.py). The event text is "A resource record of type %1, name %2 ... was created in scope %7 of zone %6", with the client IP address in %8 for 519.
falsepositives: A documented WPAD record for proxy auto-configuration (allowlist the record data in the SIEM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-DNS-Server/Audit' AND ((EventID=515 OR EventID=519) AND NAME REGEXP '(?i)^(wpad|isatap|\*)(\.|$)')
title: DNS Server Audit Record Created for wpad, isatap or Wildcard Name

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects AzureHound execution by image, PE OriginalFileName, or its specific command-line verbs. Generic Connect-MgGraph is excluded from the high-signal set because Intune and identity admins use it routinely; the network sibling azurehound_graph_api_burst.yml catches the enumeration volume instead.
falsepositives: Authorised cloud security assessment from a sanctioned host
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (Image LIKE '%\\azurehound.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='azurehound.exe' OR (CommandLine LIKE '%azurehound%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-AzureHound%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% list-available%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% list --tenant%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: AzureHound / Graph API Enumeration Tooling Execution

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write of the safe boot element (BcdOSLoaderInteger_SafeBoot, element type 0x25000080) into the Boot Configuration Data store, which Windows mounts as the registry hive HKLM\BCD00000000. Any tool that sets safeboot (bcdedit /set safeboot minimal, network or dsrepair, msconfig, the BCD WMI provider) ends up writing this value, so this is the effect-side pair of dc_safeboot_dsrepair. On a Domain Controller a safe boot means a boot into Directory Services Restore Mode or with the directory and its security tooling offline; on other hosts it is a known ransomware step to boot past endpoint protection.
falsepositives: An administrator using msconfig or bcdedit to troubleshoot a workstation in safe mode
Documented AD forest recovery on a Domain Controller (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\BCD00000000\\Objects\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Elements\\25000080\\Element' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Safe Boot Element Written to the Boot Configuration Data (Registry)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects local or remote process execution through WMI using wmic process call create or the PowerShell Invoke-WmiMethod / Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process Create path. Complements wmiexec_remote_command, which is Impacket-specific (WmiPrvSE parent with __output redirect); this rule catches the generic built-in WMI execution procedures that Impacket signature does not.
falsepositives: Administrative or software-deployment scripts that create processes via WMI (baseline the source hosts and parent processes, especially management servers)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\wmic.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%process%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%call%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%create%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((CommandLine LIKE '%Win32\_Process%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%Create%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-WmiMethod%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-CimMethod%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Process Execution via WMI (wmic / Invoke-WmiMethod Win32_Process Create)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4662 access to the thumbnailPhoto attribute of a contact object, which is where AD FS stores its Distributed Key Manager (DKM) master key, in a contact under CN=<guid>,CN=ADFS,CN=Microsoft,CN=Program Data in the domain partition. With the DKM key and the AD FS configuration database an attacker decrypts the token-signing certificate and forges SAML tokens for any federated user (Golden SAML; ADFSDump, AADInternals Export-AADIntADFSCertificates). Only the AD FS service account should read it.
falsepositives: AD FS farm installation or a new farm node joining (Install-AdfsFarm, Add-AdfsFarmNode) run by an administrator (ticketed)
An AD FS service account that is not in PLACEHOLDER_ADFS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT (add each farm's account, gMSA names include the trailing $)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND ObjectType LIKE '%5cb41ed0-0e4c-11d0-a286-00aa003049e2%' ESCAPE '\' AND Properties LIKE '%8d3bca50-1d7e-11d0-a081-00aa006c33ed%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_ADFS\_SERVICE\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: AD FS DKM Master Key Read from the Directory (Golden SAML Precursor)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a password reset on an inter-domain trust account (the account named after the other domain's NetBIOS name with a trailing "$" that holds the trust key) made by a named account rather than by the automatic 30-day trust password rotation. Setting the trust password to a known value (netdom trust /resetOneSide, Mimikatz lsadump::trust after a DCSync of the trust key, or a manual reset) lets an attacker forge inter-realm TGTs for the trust. Microsoft documents that a trust password reset logs 4716, then 4724 and/or 4742 against the trust account; 4738 is not part of that sequence.
falsepositives: Documented manual trust repair (netdom trust /resetOneSide or Reset-ADTrust style procedures after a broken secure channel), ticketed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4724 AND TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TRUST\_ACCOUNT$' ESCAPE '\') OR ((EventID=4742 AND TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TRUST\_ACCOUNT$' ESCAPE '\' AND PasswordLastSet IS NOT NULL) AND (NOT COALESCE((PasswordLastSet='-' OR PasswordLastSet=''), 0)))) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-7' AND SubjectLogonId='0x3e6'), 0)))
title: Trust Account Password Reset by a Named Account (Inter-Domain Trust Key Change)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a computer account created (4741) by an account that is not on the positive allowlist of provisioning, domain-join and Tier-0 administrator accounts. The default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota of 10 lets any authenticated user create computer accounts, and a computer account the attacker controls (Impacket addcomputer.py, PowerMad New-MachineAccount, KrbRelayUp, noPac) is the precondition for Resource-Based Constrained Delegation abuse, noPac and KrbRelayUp. The rule is also the first base of the KrbRelayUp RBCD chain correlation.
falsepositives: Help-desk staff or end users joining machines under the default quota. Add the sanctioned join and provisioning accounts (MDT, SCCM, Autopilot hybrid join connector, Tier-0 administrators) to filter_authorised_creators and set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 where possible.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4741 AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_COMPUTER\_JOIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Computer Account Created by Non-Provisioning Account (MachineAccountQuota Abuse)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects LLMNR, NBT-NS and mDNS poisoners started on a Windows host. Inveigh is the Windows-native poisoner, shipped as a .NET binary and as the PowerShell script Inveigh.ps1 with Invoke-Inveigh and Invoke-InveighRelay; Responder is a Python tool that is occasionally run on Windows. The .NET build is matched by OriginalFileName so a renamed copy still fires. The network effect of a running poisoner is llmnr_nbtns_listener_anomaly (UDP 5355 or 137 bound by a non-system process) and its file artefacts are responder_llmnr_nbtns_poisoning.
falsepositives: Authorised red team or penetration test activity
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((OriginalFileName='Inveigh.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Inveigh.dll') OR Image LIKE '%\\Inveigh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-Inveigh%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Inveigh.ps1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Inveigh-Relay.ps1%' ESCAPE '\') OR CommandLine LIKE '%Responder.py%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Inveigh or Responder Poisoner Execution on Windows

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Microsoft Defender Antivirus event 5007 (the antimalware platform configuration changed) recording the attack surface reduction rule "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem" (9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2) with a new mode of Off (0), Audit (2) or Not configured (5). Defender logs the change whatever made it (PowerShell, WMI, Group Policy), and it needs no Sysmon.
falsepositives: A staged ASR roll-out that puts the rule in Audit mode on a pilot group (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' AND (EventID=5007 AND NewValue REGEXP '(?i)\\ASR\\Rules\\9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2\s*=\s*(0x0*)?[025]\s*$')
title: Defender ASR Rule Block Credential Stealing from LSASS Turned Off (Defender Event 5007)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects scheduled task creation against a remote host via schtasks /create /s, or via the WMI PS_ScheduledTask class through Invoke-CimMethod, from the source host. Complements the Security-log rule atexec_remote_scheduled_task.yml, which sees the task on the target.
falsepositives: Software deployment and administration scripts that schedule tasks remotely (baseline the management hosts)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/create%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/s %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/tn%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-CimMethod%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%PS\_ScheduledTask%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%Register-ScheduledTask%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-CimSession%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Remote or WMI Scheduled Task Creation from the Command Line

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4662 access to the LSA secret objects that hold the domain DPAPI backup keys (G$BCKUPKEY_PREFERRED and G$BCKUPKEY_<guid>) by any principal that is not an allowlisted Domain Controller. Mimikatz lsadump::backupkeys and SharpDPAPI backupkey retrieve these keys over LSA RPC; with them an attacker can decrypt the DPAPI master key of every domain user, for ever, because the backup key is never rotated.
falsepositives: Unlikely. Domain backup key rotation or recovery by an identity administrator is rare and ticketed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND ObjectName LIKE '%BCKUPKEY%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: DPAPI Domain Backup Key Read by Non-DC Principal

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a command shell started by WmiPrvSE.exe whose command line redirects output to a loopback administrative share (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$ or \\127.0.0.1\C$) or to the Windows Temp folder. This is the shape of wmiexec-style remote execution (Impacket wmiexec with a renamed output file or another share, CrackMapExec / NetExec wmiexec, custom WMI execution tooling) that the exact wmiexec_remote_command pattern misses.
falsepositives: Credentialed vulnerability scanners and inventory tools that run commands through Win32_Process.Create and collect output from Windows\Temp (baseline the scanner service accounts and source hosts)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((ParentImage LIKE '%\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%>%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\\\127.0.0.1\\ADMIN$%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\\\127.0.0.1\\C$%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: WmiPrvSE Spawned Shell with Output Redirect to Loopback Share or Windows Temp

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a successful network logon whose NTLM sub-package is NTLM V1 or LM (4624, LmPackageName). NTLMv1 responses can be cracked to the account's NT hash or relayed with the signing and MIC protections stripped, which is why coercion attacks against a Domain Controller try to force an NTLMv1 downgrade. This rule sees the relay variant only, a coerced DC$ downgraded to NTLMv1 and relayed to a Windows server; the crack-only variant, where the attacker's listener captures the response and nothing is validated by Windows, leaves no 4624 and is not covered. Machine accounts are therefore in scope. Where NTLMv1 is still permitted, every hit is also a hygiene finding that names a client to remediate before setting LmCompatibilityLevel 5. This replaces the NTLMv1 branch that used to sit in ntlmrelayx_ldap_relay, which excluded every machine account and so missed the DC downgrade case.
falsepositives: Legacy appliances, printers and old operating systems still configured for NTLMv1 (populate filter_known_ntlmv1_clients, then remove them and set LmCompatibilityLevel 5)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND AuthenticationPackageName='NTLM' AND (LmPackageName='NTLM V1' OR LmPackageName='LM')) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName='ANONYMOUS LOGON' OR IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_NTLMV1\_CLIENT\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((KeyLength=0 AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_APP\_TIER\_HOST' ESCAPE '\'), 0))), 0)))
title: NTLMv1 or LM Network Logon (Relay Downgrade or Hygiene Finding)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a process opening an outbound connection to LDAP (389), LDAPS (636) or the Global Catalog (3268, 3269) when it is not one of the Windows components that normally speak LDAP: lsass (Netlogon and Kerberos), svchost (Group Policy and other services), mmc (dsa.msc and the other AD consoles), dsac (Active Directory Administrative Center), the AD Web Services host, the Defender for Endpoint sensor, dsregcmd (device registration), taskhostw (scheduled tasks such as certificate autoenrollment), the Configuration Manager client, and PowerShell on designated AD admin hosts. SharpHound, ADExplorer, ldapsearch ports, PowerView loaded into an unusual host process and custom .NET collectors all have to open these connections, whatever the binary is called. This is the effect-side pair of bloodhound_sharphound_collection, which matches file names and command lines.
falsepositives: Applications that authenticate users or look up directory data over LDAP (Java and web applications, VPN and Wi-Fi controllers, printers' scan-to-email servers); add their full image path to filter_windows_ldap_clients
Configuration Manager, Exchange, ADFS and Entra Connect servers (scope the rule to workstations and general servers, or allowlist their binaries)
Domain controllers themselves, where many directory services talk to the local LDAP port over a non-loopback address
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Initiated='true' AND (DestinationPort=389 OR DestinationPort=636 OR DestinationPort=3268 OR DestinationPort=3269)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\mmc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\mmc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\dsac.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\ADWS\\Microsoft.ActiveDirectory.WebServices.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\MsSense.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\dsregcmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\taskhostw.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\CCM\\CcmExec.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_LDAP\_CLIENT\_IMAGE' ESCAPE '\') OR (DestinationIp='127.0.0.1' OR DestinationIp='::1') OR ((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_AD\_ADMIN\_HOST01' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_AD\_ADMIN\_HOST02' ESCAPE '\'))), 0))))
title: LDAP or Global Catalog Connection from Non-Standard Process

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4738 user account change that turns on "Don't Expire Password" (SAM USER_DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWORD, 0x200) or "Encrypted Text Password Allowed" (SAM USER_ENCRYPTED_TEXT_PASSWORD_ALLOWED, 0x800, reversible encryption). An attacker who holds write rights over an account sets the first so a password they set or cracked keeps working, and the second so the next password change stores a reversibly encrypted copy that DCSync returns in clear text. On the 4738 page Microsoft says Encrypted Text Password Allowed "should not typically be enabled" for user accounts, and that Don't Expire Password "should be monitored for critical accounts, or all accounts if your organization does not allow this flag". The rule fires when the new SAM value has the bit and the old one did not, or when the rendered UserAccountControl change list says the flag was enabled.
falsepositives: Service account provisioning where policy still allows non-expiring passwords (document the accounts and the provisioning identity, then suppress by TargetUserName in the SIEM)
Legacy applications that need reversible encryption for CHAP or Digest authentication (rare, should be ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4738 AND ((NewUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[2367abefABEF][0-9a-fA-F]{2}$' AND (NOT COALESCE((OldUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[2367abefABEF][0-9a-fA-F]{2}$'), 0))) OR (NewUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[89a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]{2}$' AND (NOT COALESCE((OldUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[89a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]{2}$'), 0))) OR (UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2089%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2091%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Don''t Expire Password'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Encrypted Text Password Allowed'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Password Never Expires or Reversible Encryption Enabled on a User Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 5136 Value Added on gPCMachineExtensionNames or gPCUserExtensionNames of a groupPolicyContainer where the new value lists the Group Policy Preferences Scheduled Tasks client-side extension {AADCED64-746C-4633-A97C-D61349046527}. SharpGPOAbuse --AddComputerTask, pyGPOAbuse and New-GPOImmediateTask register this CSE so that every computer applying the GPO runs an immediate scheduled task as SYSTEM. Unlike gpo_delegation_modification.yml, which alerts on any extension change by an account outside the GPO admin allowlist, this rule has no account filter, so it also covers a compromised GPO administrator.
falsepositives: GPO administrators creating or editing scheduled task preference items (ticketed)
Any later edit of a GPO that already carries the Scheduled Tasks CSE, because the attribute is single-valued and the whole list is written again
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=5136 AND ObjectClass='groupPolicyContainer' AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPCMachineExtensionNames' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPCUserExtensionNames') AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\' AND AttributeValue LIKE '%{AADCED64-746C-4633-A97C-D61349046527}%' ESCAPE '\')
title: GPO Extension Names Written with the Scheduled Tasks Client-Side Extension

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a TGT issued with AES encryption and PA-ENC-TIMESTAMP pre-authentication (PreAuthType 2, the password or long-term-key path) for an account that is supposed to authenticate only with a smart card or Windows Hello for Business certificate (PreAuthType 15, 16 or 17). Rubeus asktgt /aes256 and Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth /aes256 with a stolen AES key produce exactly such a request. For an ordinary password account the same event is a normal logon, which is why the rule is limited to an explicit list of certificate-only accounts.
falsepositives: A certificate-only account that still has a usable password (smart card required not set, or a break-glass password logon). Check whether "Smart card is required for interactive logon" is set on the account.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 AND Status='0x0' AND PreAuthType=2 AND (TicketEncryptionType='0x11' OR TicketEncryptionType='0x12')) AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CERT\_ONLY\_ACCOUNT01' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CERT\_ONLY\_ACCOUNT02' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Overpass-the-Hash AES Variant - Key-Based TGT for a Certificate-Only Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Sysmon process access (EID 10) to lsass.exe with any access mask that includes PROCESS_VM_READ (0x10) or PROCESS_VM_WRITE (0x20), full access included, where the source image lives in a user-writable location (any folder in a user profile, Temp, AppData, Users\Public, PerfLogs, Downloads, Desktop, Windows\Tasks, Windows\Tracing, the spool color folder, the Recycle Bin, or directly in a drive root or in ProgramData). The test is the path and the access bits, not the file name or a fixed mask signature, so it survives renaming the tool and adding or removing unrelated access rights.
falsepositives: Software updaters and installers that run from Temp or AppData and open lsass with 0x1410 (Dropbox, Google, Visual Studio bootstrappers on workstations); add exact SourceImage and GrantedAccess pairs as filters
