Security scanners deployed to Windows\Temp (for example THOR or ASGARD agents)
Per-user tools kept in a profile folder outside AppData (portable admin utilities); add exact SourceImage paths as filters
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=10 AND (TargetImage LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND GrantedAccess REGEXP '(?i)^0x[0-9a-f]*[1235679abdef][0-9a-f]$' AND ((SourceImage LIKE '%\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\AppData\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\PerfLogs\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\Downloads\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\Desktop\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\Windows\\Tasks\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\Windows\\Tracing\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\spool\\drivers\\color\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE '%\\$Recycle.Bin\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR SourceImage REGEXP '(?i)^[a-z]:\\users\\[^\\]+\\.+$' OR SourceImage REGEXP '(?i)^[a-z]:\\(programdata\\)?[^\\]+$')))
title: LSASS Memory Access from a User-Writable Path

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects SQL Server audit records (Application log, event 33205) for the preparation steps of SQL lateral movement: EXECUTE AS LOGIN (impersonating a login such as sa through IMPERSONATE permission, PowerUpSQL Invoke-SQLAuditPrivImpersonateLogin), OPENROWSET or OPENDATASOURCE ad hoc distributed queries (used to reach another server or to read files with BULK), and linked-server creation or enabling RPC Out with sp_addlinkedserver and sp_serveroption. Command execution down a link is in the high sibling mssql_trusted_links_pivot.yml.
falsepositives: Applications and ETL jobs that use OPENROWSET or EXECUTE AS LOGIN by design (baseline by server_principal_name and application)
DBAs creating or configuring linked servers (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND ((Provider_Name LIKE 'MSSQL%' ESCAPE '\' AND EventID=33205) AND ((Data LIKE '%OPENROWSET%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%OPENDATASOURCE%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%sp\_addlinkedserver%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%sp\_serveroption%' ESCAPE '\') OR Data REGEXP '(?i)EXEC(UTE)?\s+AS\s+LOGIN'))
title: MSSQL Login Impersonation, Ad Hoc Distributed Query or Linked Server Change

'%IMPHASH=1781F06048A7E58B323F0B9259BE798B%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=233F85F2D4BC9D6521A6CAAE11A1E7F5%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=24AF2584CBF4D60BBE5C6D1B31B3BE6D%' ESCAPE '\' OR author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a command interpreter or download / proxy-execution binary started by wsmprovhost.exe, the host process for a PowerShell Remoting (WS-Man) session on the target. Evil-WinRM sessions run inside wsmprovhost, so any external program the operator starts appears as its child. PDF reference: "evil-winrm -i <ip>/<domain> -u <user> -H <hash>".
falsepositives: Legitimate PowerShell Remoting administration that starts cmd.exe or a nested powershell.exe (baseline the admin accounts and their source hosts)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (ParentImage LIKE '%\\wsmprovhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\certutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\bitsadmin.exe' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Child of the WinRM Remote Shell Host (Evil-WinRM, PowerShell Remoting)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the use step of dMSA abuse. A Kerberos ticket request made as a listed Delegated Managed Service Account (4768 for its TGT, or 4769 for a service ticket requested with its TGT) from an address that is not one of the servers authorised to run that dMSA. In BadSuccessor the operator requests the dMSA ticket from a workstation and inherits the predecessor's privileges, including those of a Domain Admin it was linked to.
falsepositives: A server running the dMSA-backed service whose address is not yet listed in filter_authorised_dmsa_host_ip
Address changes after a server rebuild or DHCP lease change
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4768 OR EventID=4769) AND TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DMSA\_ACCOUNT$%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DMSA\_HOST\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: dMSA Kerberos Authentication From Unexpected Host

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Service Control Manager 7040 event recording a start type change of the Remote Registry service. When Remote Registry is disabled (the default on Windows client editions), remote secretsdump and CrackMapExec switch it to demand start, start it to save the registry hives, and set it back afterwards, which produces two 7040 events around the dump.
falsepositives: Administrators or GPO enabling Remote Registry for management tools
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((Provider_Name='Service Control Manager' AND EventID=7040) AND (param1='Remote Registry' OR param4='RemoteRegistry'))
title: Remote Registry Service Start Type Changed

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects spoolsv.exe creating a .dll file under the printer driver store (spool\drivers\x64\3\ or spool\drivers\W32X86\3\, including the New and Old sub-folders). PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675 / CVE-2021-34527) abuses RpcAddPrinterDriverEx so that the spooler copies an attacker DLL, usually fetched from a UNC path, into this directory and then loads it as SYSTEM. The write is the step before the image load covered by printnightmare_spoolsv_dll_load.yml and accompanies PrintService event 316 (printnightmare_driver_install.yml). A legitimate driver installation produces the same write, so the rule is medium on its own.
falsepositives: Authorised printer driver installation or update by an administrator (correlate with change tickets and with PrintService 316 for a known driver name)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND (Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\spoolsv.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (TargetFilename LIKE '%\\spool\\drivers\\x64\\3\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\spool\\drivers\\W32X86\\3\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND TargetFilename LIKE '%.dll' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Print Spooler Writing a DLL into the Printer Driver Directory

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Set-MpPreference called with -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids where the command line does not contain the GUID of the attack surface reduction rule "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem" (9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2). Microsoft documents that Set-MpPreference overwrites any existing ASR rules and their modes with the values given, so such a command drops the LSASS rule from the local configuration without ever naming it. Add-MpPreference adds rules without touching existing ones and is not matched.
falsepositives: Endpoint administrators setting the full ASR rule list on a host where the LSASS rule is deliberately not deployed, for example where LSA protection or Credential Guard already protects LSASS (ticketed; suppress by Computer)
A host where the LSASS rule was never configured locally, so the overwrite removes nothing (the rule cannot see the previous list)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%Set-MpPreference%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%ReductionRules\_I%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Defender ASR Rule List Overwritten with Set-MpPreference Without the LSASS Rule

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects enumeration of stored credentials in the Windows Credential Manager and Credential Vault using signed built-in utilities (vaultcmd, cmdkey) or the PasswordVault API. Operators run this to harvest saved RDP, web, and domain credentials without dropping a tool. Keyed on the command behaviour, not a binary name, so it survives a rename.
falsepositives: Help-desk or backup tooling that enumerates saved credentials (baseline the accounts and hosts that legitimately do this)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%vaultcmd /list%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%vaultcmd.exe /list%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cmdkey /list%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Get-VaultCredential%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Windows.Security.Credentials.PasswordVault%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Windows Credential Manager / Vault Enumeration

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a user or computer account change that enables the PASSWD_NOTREQD flag ('Password Not Required' - Enabled, message %%2082 in the UserAccountControl field of 4738 and 4742), and a computer account created with the flag (4741), which is how a "pre-Windows 2000 compatible" computer object is created. Basis of nxc pre2k abuse, where such a computer account's password equals its lowercase short name.
falsepositives: Legacy accounts intentionally configured this way (inventory and remediate)
Computer accounts pre-staged in Active Directory Users and Computers before the machine joins (confirm the account later joins and the flag is cleared)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4738 OR EventID=4741 OR EventID=4742) AND (UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2082%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Password Not Required'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Account With PASSWD_NOTREQD Set (pre2k Abuse)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects access to Groups.xml / Services.xml / DataSources.xml in SYSVOL which may contain the legacy encrypted cpassword attribute (MS14-025). The effect counterpart that does not need process telemetry is the 5145 correlation gpp_preference_xml_bulk_read.yml. PDF reference: "findstr /S /I cpassword \\<FQDN>\sysvol\<FQDN>\policies\*.xml".
falsepositives: GPO documentation tooling
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%cpassword%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Get-GPPPassword%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%gpp-decrypt%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%smb\_enum\_gpp%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Groups.xml%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Services.xml%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ScheduledTasks.xml%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%DataSources.xml%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%sysvol%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%Policies%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.xml%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Group Policy Preferences cpassword Access in SYSVOL

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects AS-REP Roasting where the attacker accepts an AES-encrypted AS-REP (0x11 AES128 or 0x12 AES256). A successful 4768 TGT request issued without Kerberos pre-authentication (PreAuthType 0) still yields an offline-crackable blob, only slower to crack than RC4. This is the path left when RC4 is disabled for the account or domain, and the path taken by Rubeus asreproast /aes. Sibling of asrep_roasting_4768_preauth (RC4).
falsepositives: Legitimate logons by accounts intentionally configured without pre-authentication, which on a modern domain use AES (inventory them and remove the flag)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4768 AND Status='0x0' AND PreAuthType=0 AND (TicketEncryptionType='0x11' OR TicketEncryptionType='0x12'))
title: AS-REP Roasting with AES Ticket Encryption

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the source-host artefact of Pass-the-Hash on Windows: 4624 LogonType 9 (NewCredentials) from the Secondary Logon service (seclogo) with AuthenticationPackageName Negotiate or NTLM. This is the runas /netonly, Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth and Rubeus createnetonly signature. It does not see Linux-origin PtH (xfreerdp /pth, impacket -hashes), which produces no event on the attacker host; the target-side NTLM logon for those is covered by ntlmrelayx_ldap_relay.yml. The rule does not detect the spawned child process; pair it with process-creation telemetry for that.
falsepositives: Legitimate runas /netonly use by administrators (review SubjectUserName)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=9 AND LogonProcessName LIKE 'seclogo%' ESCAPE '\' AND (AuthenticationPackageName='Negotiate' OR AuthenticationPackageName='NTLM'))
title: Pass-the-Hash Source-Host Logon (LogonType 9 NewCredentials via Secondary Logon)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DNS queries originating from lsass.exe or wmiprvse.exe to non-AD domains. Possible covert C2 staged through injected modules. Requires Sysmon EID 22.
falsepositives: Authorised auth integrations resolving SaaS endpoints
Additional internal DNS suffixes (add them to the filter explicitly; generic suffixes such as .local and .corp were removed because attacker infrastructure can use them too)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=22 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\wmiprvse.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((QueryName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN' ESCAPE '\' OR QueryName LIKE '%.PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN' ESCAPE '\') OR (Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (QueryName='login.microsoftonline.com' OR QueryName='login.windows.net' OR QueryName='device.login.microsoftonline.com' OR QueryName='enterpriseregistration.windows.net'))), 0))))
title: Anomalous DNS Query from LSASS or WMIPrvSE

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4739 domain policy change that writes a weak value. Account lockout threshold set to 0 (no lockout, which opens the domain to password spraying), password complexity turned off or reversible encryption turned on for the whole domain (PasswordProperties 0, 16 or 17), minimum password length set below the Windows default of 7, password history set to 0, or ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota raised above the default of 10. Microsoft's guidance for 4739 is to alert on any unplanned change to the lockout or password policy. Only events logged by a Domain Controller are matched.
falsepositives: A deliberate policy decision, for example dropping complexity in favour of long passphrases with a banned-password list (ticketed; suppress the exact field and value afterwards)
Lab or freshly built domains
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4739 AND (Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\')) AND (LockoutThreshold=0 OR (PasswordProperties=0 OR PasswordProperties=16 OR PasswordProperties=17) OR MinPasswordLength REGEXP '^[0-6]$' OR PasswordHistoryLength=0 OR MachineAccountQuota REGEXP '^(1[1-9]|[2-9][0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2,})$'))
title: Domain Password or Lockout Policy Weakened

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Sysmon file creation (EID 11) of a file named ntds.dit or ntds.jfm outside the live NTDS folder, or of a file named SYSTEM outside Windows\System32\config. Offline NTDS theft needs the database and the SYSTEM hive (for the boot key) side by side; ntdsutil IFM writes both into its media folder ("Active Directory\ntds.dit" and "registry\SYSTEM"), and shadow-copy and esentutl copies write them wherever the operator chooses.
falsepositives: Documented IFM media creation for DC promotion by Tier-0 admins
Backup or imaging tools that stage the SYSTEM hive as a file named SYSTEM
In-place OS upgrades that write hive copies under $WINDOWS.~BT or Windows.old (add the exact full path if seen, never a folder prefix)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND (((TargetFilename LIKE '%\\ntds.dit' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\ntds.jfm' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\NTDS\\ntds.dit' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\NTDS\\ntds.jfm' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_NTDS\_DIRntds.dit' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_NTDS\_DIRntds.jfm' ESCAPE '\') OR ((TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntds.dit%' ESCAPE '\') AND (Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\servicing\\TrustedInstaller.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\%\\TiWorker.exe' ESCAPE '\'))), 0))) OR (TargetFilename LIKE '%\\SYSTEM' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\config\\RegBack\\SYSTEM' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: NTDS.dit, ntds.jfm or SYSTEM Hive Written Outside Its Home Path

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects an SPN written onto a user account (5136 on servicePrincipalName), the setup step for targeted Kerberoasting. Filtering uses a positive allowlist of the accounts that legitimately manage SPNs, not a machine-account wildcard, because an operator with machine-account context (RBCD, dMSA, S4U) could otherwise write the SPN under a $ account and evade the rule.
falsepositives: Application onboarding that legitimately registers SPNs (populate filter_authorised_spn_managers)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='servicePrincipalName' AND ObjectClass='user') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_SPN\_ADMIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_APP\_ONBOARDING\_SVC' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Targeted Kerberoasting via servicePrincipalName Write on a User

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DPAPI master-key extraction or decryption. Tooling: mimikatz dpapi::masterkey / dpapi::cred, SharpDPAPI machinemasterkeys / triage. PDF reference: "dpapi extract".
falsepositives: Unlikely
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%dpapi::masterkey%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%dpapi::cred%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%dpapi::chrome%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%dpapi::vault%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%SharpDPAPI%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%SharpChrome%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%machinemasterkeys%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/rpc /target:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsadump::backupkeys%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: DPAPI MasterKey Decryption via Mimikatz or SharpDPAPI

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects 7045 service installs that combine a staging-directory binary path with a random-looking eight-character alphanumeric service name, the shape C2 frameworks such as Sliver and Havoc produce when an operator stages a service binary in a writable folder and lets the tool pick the name. Requiring both the path and the random-name pattern keeps this distinct from psexec_service_install.yml (whose random binaries sit directly in %systemroot%) and cuts false positives from legitimate ProgramData services.
falsepositives: Rare legitimate installers using random service names in ProgramData (baseline and exclude vendors)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((EventID=7045 AND (ImagePath LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\ProgramData\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\PerfLogs\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\Recovery\\%' ESCAPE '\')) AND ServiceName REGEXP '^[a-zA-Z0-9]{8}$')
title: Service Install with Random Name from Temp/ProgramData (Sliver/Havoc)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Certificate Services backup on the CA (4876 backup started, 4877 backup completed) by an account that is not an approved PKI administrator or backup identity. Microsoft's Securing PKI events appendix files both events under backing up and restoring the CA database (certutil -backupDB, the database part of certutil -backup, or the Certification Authority console backup wizard). The same operator action often includes a CA key backup (certutil -backup, or the wizard's private key option); whoever holds that key can forge a certificate for any principal (Golden Certificate) that survives password resets and is valid until the CA certificate expires.
falsepositives: Scheduled CA backups run by an identity not yet in filter_pki_admins
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4876 OR EventID=4877) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN01' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN02' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_BACKUP\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Certificate Services Database Backup Started or Completed by a Non-PKI Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the Entra seamless SSO computer account AZUREADSSOACC$ acting as an authenticating principal on premises: a TGT request (4768), a failed pre-authentication (4771), an NTLM validation (4776), a logon (4624, 4625) whose account is AZUREADSSOACC$, or a service ticket request (4769) made by AZUREADSSOACC$ as the client. The account represents Microsoft Entra ID in the forest; browsers request service tickets FOR it, but no host logs on AS it. An attacker who has taken its key with DCSync can use it like any computer account hash (overpass-the-hash or pass-the-hash), which this rule sees.
falsepositives: Unlikely. No Microsoft-documented process authenticates as this account
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4624 OR EventID=4625 OR EventID=4768 OR EventID=4771 OR EventID=4776) AND TargetUserName='AZUREADSSOACC$') OR (EventID=4769 AND TargetUserName LIKE 'AZUREADSSOACC$@%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Seamless SSO Computer Account AZUREADSSOACC$ Used to Authenticate

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects WinPEAS, PowerUp.ps1, Seatbelt and Invoke-PrivEsc execution. PDF reference: "Privilege escalation / Low access / winpeas.exe".
falsepositives: Sanctioned internal assessments
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\winpeas.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\winpeasx64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\winpeasx86.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\linpeas.sh' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\Seatbelt.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%winpeas%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-PowerUp%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-AllChecks%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Seatbelt -group=all%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%PrivescCheck.ps1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-PrivescAudit%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: WinPEAS / PowerUp Local Privilege Escalation Enumeration

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the SilentProcessExit credential-dump technique: an attacker registers lsass.exe for silent-exit monitoring so that WerFault writes a full memory dump on a triggered exit, recovering credentials without ever calling OpenProcess on lsass. This evades access-mask and handle-based LSASS rules entirely; the only reliable signal is the registry configuration itself.
falsepositives: Legitimate debugging configuration of lsass by Microsoft support (rare; verify the operator and the dump folder)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\SilentProcessExit\\lsass.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Image File Execution Options\\lsass.exe%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\GlobalFlag' ESCAPE '\')))
title: LSASS Dump via SilentProcessExit / WerFault Registry Abuse

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Rubeus command-line patterns: asktgt, ptt, ptc, createnetonly, asktgs, tgtdeleg, kerberoast, asreproast. PDF reference: multiple Rubeus examples (asktgt /user, ptt /ticket, createnetonly /program).
falsepositives: Authorised red team activity
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%Rubeus.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% asktgt /user:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% asktgs %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ptt /ticket%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ptt /luid%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ptc %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% createnetonly %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% kerberoast%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% asreproast%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% tgtdeleg%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% renew /ticket:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% dump /service:krbtgt%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% dump /luid:%' ESCAPE '\') OR OriginalFileName='Rubeus.exe'))
title: Rubeus Pass-the-Ticket / Ask-TGT Indicators

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects secretsdump.py execution patterns on a Windows foothold: SAM, SECURITY and SYSTEM remote registry save followed by file pull, or direct DCSync. These strings appear only when the tool runs on Windows; the usual case is secretsdump run from a Linux host, which leaves nothing here. The target-side artefacts are covered by secretsdump_remote_hive_save_tmp_file (Sysmon 11), remote_registry_winreg_pipe_access (5145) and remote_registry_service_start_type_changed (7040), and the DCSync mode by dcsync_drsuapi_replication. PDF reference: "secretsdump.py <DOMAIN>/<MACHINE>$@<IP> -no-pass -just-dc-user 'Administrator'".
falsepositives: Unlikely
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%secretsdump.py%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%secretsdump %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-just-dc%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-just-dc-user%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-just-dc-ntlm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-no-pass%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%restorepassword.py%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Impacket secretsdump.py Indicators

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects file artefacts of Responder or Inveigh running on a Windows host (Responder-Session.log, Responder.db, Responder.conf; Inveigh-Log.txt, Inveigh-NTLMv1.txt, Inveigh-NTLMv2.txt and the other Inveigh outputs). The UDP listener precondition (a non-system process bound to 5355/137) is covered by the sibling network rule llmnr_nbtns_listener_anomaly.yml, and the tool start by inveigh_responder_process_execution. PDF reference: "responder -i eth0".
falsepositives: Authorised red team activity
Security researchers unpacking the Responder source tree on an analysis workstation
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND ((TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Responder-Session.log%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Responder.db%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Responder.conf%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Responder.py%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%Responder\\logs\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-Log.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-NTLMv1.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-NTLMv2.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-Cleartext.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-FormInput.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-NTLMv1Users.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\Inveigh-NTLMv2Users.txt' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Responder LLMNR / NBT-NS Poisoning Indicators

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a process other than the Windows name-resolution owners receiving inbound traffic on UDP 5355 (LLMNR) or 137 (NBT-NS), which is the precondition for Responder, Inveigh or a similar poisoner running on a Windows host (the attacker-side view). On Windows, LLMNR is served by the DNS Client service in svchost.exe and NBT-NS by the NetBT driver, which Sysmon reports as the image "System". The victim-side view is llmnr_response_from_unexpected_host; tool execution and tool artefacts are inveigh_responder_process_execution and responder_llmnr_nbtns_poisoning.
falsepositives: Custom name-resolution responders or virtualisation network agents bound to UDP 5355 or 137 (rare on Windows servers)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Initiated='false' AND (DestinationPort=5355 OR DestinationPort=137)) AND (NOT COALESCE((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image='System'), 0))))
title: LLMNR / NBT-NS Poisoning via Suspicious UDP Listener

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Impacket smbexec, which obtains semi-interactive command execution by repeatedly creating a temporary Windows service whose ImagePath runs a command via the command interpreter. The ImagePath echoes the operator command into a batch file, runs the batch file with output redirected to a share file named __output, and deletes it. Distinct from psexec (which drops a service binary): smbexec leaves no binary. Two branches, either of which fires. The classic "/Q /c" plus __output redirect, and the echo-to-batch-file structure, which survives a renamed output file. PDF reference: "wmiexec.py / atexec.py / smbexec.py -hashes ':<hash>' <user>@<ip>".
falsepositives: Rare. Legitimate software almost never installs a service whose ImagePath echoes a command into a batch file and deletes it, or pipes interpreter output to a __output share file.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (EventID=7045 AND (((ImagePath LIKE '%/Q /c%' ESCAPE '\' AND ImagePath LIKE '%\_\_output%' ESCAPE '\') AND (ImagePath LIKE '%\%COMSPEC\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%cmd.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\127.0.0.1\\%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (ImagePath LIKE '%/Q /c echo %' ESCAPE '\' AND ImagePath LIKE '%.bat%' ESCAPE '\' AND ImagePath LIKE '%& del %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Impacket smbexec Service Command Execution

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects step one of ESC3. A certificate request (4886) or issuance (4887) against an enrollment-agent template (Certificate Request Agent EKU, 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.1) by a Requester that is not an approved PKI administrator or enrollment-agent operator. An enrollment-agent certificate lets its holder request certificates on behalf of any user, including Domain Admins, through any template that accepts agent co-signing.
falsepositives: Smart card issuance staff enrolling for their agent certificate who are not yet in filter_pki_admins
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4886 OR EventID=4887) AND Attributes REGEXP '(?i)(^|\n)CertificateTemplate:(EnrollmentAgent|EnrollmentAgentOffline|MachineEnrollmentAgent|PLACEHOLDER_ENROLLMENT_AGENT_TEMPLATE)\r?(\n|$)') AND (NOT COALESCE((Requester LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN01' ESCAPE '\' OR Requester LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN02' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Enrollment Agent Certificate Requested by a Non-PKI Account (ESC3)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects mimikatz misc::skeleton execution which patches LSASS in-memory to accept the master password "mimikatz" for any account. PDF reference: "mimikatz 'privilege::debug' 'misc::skeleton' 'exit'". Command-line rule, capped at high; the paired effect rule is lsass_process_access_credential_dump (Sysmon 10 GrantedAccess 0x1438 on lsass, the read-write access the patch needs).
falsepositives: Unlikely
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%misc::skeleton%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%"misc::skeleton"%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%kerberos::skeleton%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Mimikatz Skeleton Key Persistence

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects renamed offensive tooling: a process whose PE version resource (OriginalFileName, FileDescription, Product or Company, as Sysmon EID 1 reports them) names a known offensive binary while the Image file name has been changed. Defeats trivial "Move-Item Rubeus.exe ./svchost.exe" rename bypasses, including GhostPack builds whose OriginalFileName was edited but whose assembly title and product were left at the project name.
falsepositives: Authorised red team activity where renamed binaries are sanctioned
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (((OriginalFileName='Rubeus.exe' OR OriginalFileName='mimikatz.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpHound.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpHound.dll' OR OriginalFileName='PowerSploit.dll' OR OriginalFileName='Seatbelt.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpUp.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpSpray.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpDPAPI.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpChrome.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Certify.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Whisker.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SafetyKatz.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpKatz.exe' OR OriginalFileName='nanodump.exe' OR OriginalFileName='PPLdump64.exe' OR OriginalFileName='WinPEAS.exe' OR OriginalFileName='psexec.c') OR ((Description='Rubeus' OR Description='SharpHound' OR Description='Seatbelt' OR Description='SharpUp' OR Description='SharpDPAPI' OR Description='SharpChrome' OR Description='Certify' OR Description='SafetyKatz' OR Description='SharpWMI' OR Description='mimikatz for Windows') OR (Product='Rubeus' OR Product='SharpHound' OR Product='Seatbelt' OR Product='SharpUp' OR Product='SharpDPAPI' OR Product='SharpChrome' OR Product='Certify' OR Product='SafetyKatz' OR Product='SharpWMI' OR Product='mimikatz') OR Company='gentilkiwi (Benjamin DELPY)')) AND (NOT COALESCE((Image LIKE '%\\Rubeus.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\mimikatz.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\SharpHound.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\Seatbelt.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\Certify.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\PsExec.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\PsExec64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\WinPEAS.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Renamed Known Offensive Tool via PE Metadata Mismatch

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a password reset of the Entra seamless SSO computer account AZUREADSSOACC$ (4724, or 4742 with PasswordLastSet changed) by any account other than the administrator who performs the sanctioned Kerberos decryption key rollover. Whoever sets this password knows the key that Entra ID trusts for seamless SSO tickets once it is synced. Microsoft recommends rolling the key over every 30 days with Update-AzureADSSOForest, run with domain administrator credentials, so an expected reset is periodic and made by a known person.
falsepositives: The monthly key rollover run by an administrator who is not in PLACEHOLDER_ENTRA_SSO_ROLLOVER_ADMIN (add every person who runs Update-AzureADSSOForest)
Re-enabling seamless SSO in Entra Connect, which recreates the account and sets its password
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4724 AND TargetUserName='AZUREADSSOACC$') OR ((EventID=4742 AND TargetUserName='AZUREADSSOACC$' AND PasswordLastSet IS NOT NULL) AND (NOT COALESCE((PasswordLastSet='-' OR PasswordLastSet=''), 0)))) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_ENTRA\_SSO\_ROLLOVER\_ADMIN' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Seamless SSO Computer Account AZUREADSSOACC$ Password Reset Outside Rollover

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects an interactive (LogonType 2), unlock or reconnect (7) or Remote Desktop (10) logon on a Tier-0 server (domain controller, certification authority, Entra Connect server) whose source is not a privileged access workstation. In a tiered administration model Tier-0 servers are reached only from PAWs, so an interactive session from any other address means a broken tiering rule or an attacker using Tier-0 credentials from a compromised lower-tier host.
falsepositives: Console (LogonType 2) logons at a DC through a hypervisor or out-of-band console during break-glass work. These carry IpAddress 127.0.0.1 or "-" and always alert; record them as approved changes.
A PAW missing from the allowlist, or a PAW whose address changed (use DHCP reservations or a fixed PAW subnet)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND (LogonType=2 OR LogonType=7 OR LogonType=10)) AND (Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TIER0\_HOST01\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TIER0\_HOST02\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_TIER0\_HOST03\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' OR Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_SERVER\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetDomainName='Window Manager' OR TargetDomainName='Font Driver Host'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_PAW\_IP01' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_PAW\_IP02' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Interactive or RDP Logon to a Tier-0 Server from a Non-PAW Source

author: 404secnotfound
description: Security log equivalent of lsass_anomalous_child_process for hosts without Sysmon. Detects event 4688 (a new process has been created) whose ParentProcessName is lsass.exe and whose NewProcessName is anything other than Windows Error Reporting. Requires Audit Process Creation; the ParentProcessName field is present from Windows 10 and Server 2016.
falsepositives: Unconfirmed. LSASS may start efsui.exe for Encrypting File System prompts; add its full System32 path to the filter if it appears in your baseline
Patch installation events (rare)
Third-party authentication packages that start a helper process (add the exact NewProcessName after review)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4688 AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\WerFault.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\WerFaultSecure.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Anomalous Child Process Spawned by LSASS (Security 4688)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the command lines that take the CA private key off a Certification Authority. certutil -backupKey, -backupDB or -backup anywhere, or certutil -exportPFX on the CA host, run by an account that is not an approved PKI administrator, and, from any account, SharpDPAPI "certificates /machine" and the mimikatz crypto module key export commands that read machine private keys directly and bypass the CA backup audit. Paired effect rules are adcs_ca_backup_or_key_export.yml (4876, 4877) and adcs_ca_key_file_written.yml (Sysmon 11 .p12 or .pfx).
falsepositives: Scheduled CA backups run by an identity not yet in filter_pki_admins
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (((Image LIKE '%\\certutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='CertUtil.exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%-backupkey%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/backupkey%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-backupdb%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/backupdb%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-backup %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/backup %' ESCAPE '\') OR ((CommandLine LIKE '%-exportpfx%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/exportpfx%' ESCAPE '\') AND Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_SERVER\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((User LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN01' ESCAPE '\' OR User LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_PKI\_ADMIN02' ESCAPE '\' OR User LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_BACKUP\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR ((CommandLine LIKE '%certificates%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/machine%' ESCAPE '\') AND (Image LIKE '%\\SharpDPAPI.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='SharpDPAPI.exe')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%crypto::capi%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%crypto::cng%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%crypto::certificates%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: CA Private Key or Database Backup and Machine Certificate Export Tooling

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects SQL Server audit records (Application log, event 33205) whose statement runs operating-system commands or forces an outbound SMB authentication: xp_cmdshell (direct, enabled through sp_configure, or sent down a trusted linked-server chain with EXEC (...) AT [link] or OPENQUERY as mssql_link_crawler and PowerUpSQL Get-SQLServerLinkCrawl do), sp_OACreate / sp_OAMethod OLE automation, and xp_dirtree, xp_subdirs or xp_fileexist against a UNC path, which makes the SQL Server service account authenticate to an attacker host for relay or cracking. Impersonation and linked-server setup statements are in the medium sibling mssql_linked_server_impersonation.yml. PDF reference: "exploit/windows/mssql/mssql_link_crawler".
falsepositives: Legacy SQL Agent jobs or maintenance scripts that still use xp_cmdshell or OLE automation (baseline by server_principal_name in the audit record)
Backup scripts that probe a UNC backup share with xp_fileexist or xp_dirtree (allowlist the share host in the SIEM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND ((Provider_Name LIKE 'MSSQL%' ESCAPE '\' AND EventID=33205) AND ((Data LIKE '%xp\_cmdshell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%sp\_OACreate%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%sp\_OAMethod%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((Data LIKE '%xp\_dirtree%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%xp\_subdirs%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%xp\_fileexist%' ESCAPE '\') AND (Data LIKE '%\\\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%''//%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%CHAR(92)%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: MSSQL OS Command Execution, OLE Automation or UNC Coercion (SQL Server Audit)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the first step of noPac / sAMAccountName spoofing (CVE-2021-42278 and CVE-2021-42287). An account renames a computer account (4781 with an old name ending in "$") to a name without the trailing "$", typically the short name of a Domain Controller, so that a TGT can be requested for that name and the KDC later falls back to the DC machine account during S4U2self. Legitimate tooling never removes the "$" from a computer sAMAccountName, so the single event is high fidelity on its own. Patched DCs (KB5008102) reject the rename and the event does not appear, so a hit also means a DC is missing the November 2021 hardening.
falsepositives: Unlikely. A user account whose old name happened to end in "$" being renamed to a plain name (hidden-user clean-up) also matches; confirm the object class.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4781 AND OldTargetUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' AND NewTargetUserName REGEXP '[^$]$')
title: Computer Account sAMAccountName Renamed Without Trailing Dollar (noPac)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects changes to certificate template objects that introduce ESC-class vulnerabilities: enrollment flags, name flags, EKU, or the template DACL. A single 5136 selection on pKICertificateTemplate attribute writes closes ESC2, ESC4, ESC9, ESC10 and ESC15 misconfiguration paths.
falsepositives: Authorised PKI administration during template lifecycle changes (rare, ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=5136 AND ObjectClass='pKICertificateTemplate' AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msPKI-Enrollment-Flag' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='pKIExtendedKeyUsage' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msPKI-Certificate-Application-Policy'))
title: ADCS Certificate Template Security or Flag Modification (ESC2/4/9/10/15)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the registry values that turn off LSASS protection being set to 0. RunAsPPL under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa disables added LSA protection (LSASS as a protected process); LsaCfgFlags under the same key or under the DeviceGuard policy key disables Credential Guard; and EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity 0 turns off the virtualization-based security that Credential Guard runs in (at the DeviceGuard control key or the DeviceGuard policy key). Each takes effect at the next boot and re-opens LSASS memory to Mimikatz-style credential dumping. Microsoft documents setting these values to 0 as the way to disable both features.
falsepositives: Troubleshooting an LSA plug-in or smart card driver that is incompatible with LSA protection or Credential Guard (ticketed; such hosts should be few and named)
A Group Policy that deliberately turns Credential Guard off on a server class (the write is made by the Group Policy client, so check the GPO change history)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\Lsa\\RunAsPPL' ESCAPE '\' OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\Lsa\\LsaCfgFlags' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\DeviceGuard\\LsaCfgFlags' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\DeviceGuard\\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\DeviceGuard\\EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity' ESCAPE '\')) AND (Details='DWORD (0x00000000)' OR Details=0)))
title: LSA Protection or Credential Guard Disabled in the Registry

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a user (4738) or computer (4742) account change that configures Kerberos delegation. Either AllowedToDelegateTo is populated with services (constrained delegation; the field shows "-" when the attribute did not change and "<value not set>", raw %%1793, when the list is empty or was cleared), or the userAccountControl change text shows TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION (0x80000, unconstrained) or TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION (0x1000000, protocol transition) being enabled. Attackers who hold SeEnableDelegationPrivilege or write access set unconstrained delegation on a host they own, then coerce a Domain Controller to it to capture its TGT.
falsepositives: Domain Controller promotion, which enables TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION on the new DC computer account (correlate with the server trust account change in the same event)
Documented delegation configuration for application servers (IIS to SQL), ticketed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4738 OR EventID=4742) AND ((AllowedToDelegateTo IS NOT NULL AND (NOT COALESCE((AllowedToDelegateTo='-' OR AllowedToDelegateTo='' OR AllowedToDelegateTo LIKE '\%\%1793' ESCAPE '\' OR AllowedToDelegateTo='<value not set>'), 0))) OR (UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2093%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2098%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Trusted For Delegation'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Trusted To Authenticate For Delegation'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[2367abefABEF][0-9a-fA-F]{3}$' AND (NOT COALESCE((OldUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[2367abefABEF][0-9a-fA-F]{3}$'), 0))) OR (NewUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[4-7c-fC-F][0-9a-fA-F]{4}$' AND (NOT COALESCE((OldUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[4-7c-fC-F][0-9a-fA-F]{4}$'), 0)))))
title: Kerberos Delegation Configured on User or Computer Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects classic Kerberoasting via successful 4769 service ticket requests (Status 0x0) where the ticket encryption type is RC4-HMAC (0x17). Tooling: GetUserSPNs.py, Rubeus kerberoast, kerberoast.exe. Failed TGS requests are ignored because they return no crackable ticket. The encryption-agnostic sibling is kerberoast_distinct_spn_burst (many distinct services from one account). PDF reference: "GetUserSPNs.py -request -dc-ip ..." and "Rubeus kerberoast".
falsepositives: Legacy applications whose service account still only supports RC4 (list the service account names in filter_legacy_rc4_services after an inventory)
Trusts to older domains that downgrade encryption
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 AND Status='0x0' AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17') AND (NOT COALESCE((ServiceName='krbtgt' OR ServiceName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_LEGACY\_RC4\_SERVICE\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Kerberoasting via RC4 TGS Requests

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Sysmon image load (EID 7) of a dbghelp.dll or dbgcore.dll copy whose own path is in Windows\Temp, a user Temp folder, Users\Public, Downloads, Desktop or PerfLogs. Windows loads these DLLs from System32; a private copy in a writable folder is what dumping tools that bundle their own MiniDumpWriteDump provider, and DLL side-loading through a planted dbghelp.dll, look like. The test uses OriginalFileName as well as the file name, so a renamed copy still matches. Critical branch of dbghelp_loaded_by_non_wer_process.
falsepositives: Installer bootstrappers that extract a bundled dbghelp.dll into Temp and load it for their own crash handling (add the exact Image and ImageLoaded pair as a filter after review)
Portable debugging tools run from Downloads or Desktop by developers
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=7 AND (((ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\dbghelp.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\dbgcore.dll' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='dbghelp.dll' OR OriginalFileName='dbghelp.dll.mui' OR OriginalFileName='dbgcore.dll' OR OriginalFileName='dbgcore.dll.mui')) AND (ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Downloads\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Desktop\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\PerfLogs\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: dbghelp.dll / dbgcore.dll Loaded from a Temp or User Folder

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the named pipe that SeImpersonate escalation tools create to catch a SYSTEM connection. PrintSpoofer creates \\.\pipe\<random>\pipe\spoolss and coerces the spooler to connect to \\host/pipe/<random>, which the path normaliser turns into that nested name. RoguePotato listens on \\.\pipe\RoguePotato\pipe\epmapper by default, and GodPotato and EfsPotato use the same nested form with epmapper or another RPC endpoint name. Sysmon event 17 records the name without the \\.\pipe prefix, so the nested form appears as a second "\pipe\" inside PipeName. The rule does not depend on the tool name or the command line.
falsepositives: Software that names its pipes with an embedded "\pipe\" segment (none known; baseline Sysmon 17 for a week before routing)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND ((EventID=17 OR EventID=18) AND (PipeName LIKE '%\\pipe\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR PipeName LIKE '%RoguePotato%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potato or PrintSpoofer Nested Named Pipe Created

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Impacket atexec.py and equivalent tradecraft via the Security log: a scheduled task created (4698) or updated (4702) whose action runs a command interpreter with output redirected to the ADMIN$ share or a Temp path. The on-host schtasks /s and WMI PS_ScheduledTask variants are covered by the sibling process_creation rule remote_scheduled_task_creation_cli.yml. This rule was split from a mixed-source rule whose 4688 branches could never match 4698 events. PDF reference: "atexec.py -hashes ':<hash>' <user>@<ip>".
falsepositives: Authorised remote task management that writes to Windows\Temp (baseline the admin accounts)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4698 OR EventID=4702) AND (((TaskContent LIKE '%<Command>cmd.exe</Command>%' ESCAPE '\' OR TaskContent LIKE '%<Command>\%COMSPEC\%</Command>%' ESCAPE '\' OR TaskContent LIKE '%<Command>C:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe</Command>%' ESCAPE '\') AND (TaskContent LIKE '%> \%windir\%\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TaskContent LIKE '%> C:\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TaskContent LIKE '%> \\\\127.0.0.1\\%' ESCAPE '\')) OR TaskName REGEXP '^\\[a-zA-Z]{8}$'))
title: Remote Scheduled Task Created for One-Shot Command Execution (atexec)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the read step of dMSA abuse. A 4662 directory-service access on the msDS-ManagedPassword attribute of a Delegated Managed Service Account object (ObjectType is the msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount class) by a principal that is not on the positive allowlist of hosts authorised to retrieve the dMSA password. After BadSuccessor an attacker who added itself to the dMSA's retrieval principals can read the managed password blob directly over LDAP.
falsepositives: Hosts that run the dMSA-backed service and are not yet listed in filter_authorised_dmsa_hosts (populate it from msDS-GroupMSAMembership)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND ObjectType LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_DMSA\_CLASS\_SCHEMA\_GUID%' ESCAPE '\' AND Properties LIKE '%e362ed86-b728-0842-b27d-2dea7a9df218%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DMSA\_HOST01$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: dMSA msDS-ManagedPassword Read by Unauthorised Principal

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a network logon (4624 LogonType 3) as a Domain Controller machine account from an IP address that does not belong to that Domain Controller. A DC authenticates as itself only from its own addresses. A logon as DC01$ from anywhere else is the footprint of relayed or stolen DC machine credentials (coercion plus NTLM relay, or a forged or stolen DC ticket), which an attacker uses to DCSync under the DC identity. The DCSync rule cannot see this case because its positive allowlist must contain DC01$.
falsepositives: A DC address missing from its own filter (a second NIC, an IPv6 global or link-local address, a new IP after re-addressing)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3) AND ((TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1' OR IpAddress='-'), 0))) OR (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1' OR IpAddress='-'), 0)))))
title: DC Machine Account Network Logon from a Non-DC Address (Relay to DCSync)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write to the Windows Update policy values WUServer, WUStatusServer or UseWUServer outside a Group Policy refresh. Redirecting a client to a rogue or compromised WSUS server (WSUSpect, WSUSpendu, mitm WSUS over HTTP) lets an attacker push signed Microsoft binaries such as PsExec with attacker-chosen arguments. Legitimate changes arrive through Group Policy (svchost.exe hosting gpsvc), so a write by any other image is the signal. Tool indicators are in the sibling process_creation rule wsus_wsuspendu_tooling.yml. This rule was rewritten from a mixed-source rule whose command-line and registry branches referenced fields that do not exist in the Windows Update log.
falsepositives: Sanctioned WSUS configuration changes applied by configuration management agents rather than Group Policy (baseline the agent image)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\WUServer' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\WUStatusServer' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\AU\\UseWUServer' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: WSUS Client Update Server Redirected via Registry

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a certificate request or issuance (4886, 4887) whose Attributes carry a Subject Alternative Name as a request attribute ("SAN:upn=...", "SAN:dns=...", or the SID extension OID), against a template that is not on the list of templates allowed to take an enrollee-supplied subject. A CA only honours a SAN request attribute when EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 is set (ESC6), so on a hardened CA this should never appear, and on a vulnerable CA it is how Certipy and certreq ask for a certificate as another principal. ESC1 puts the SAN inside the CSR, which 4886 and 4887 do not render. On the KDC side an ESC1 certificate without a SID extension can surface as KB5014754 event 39 (adcs_kdc_certificate_weak_mapping.yml); one carrying the target's SID in the SAN URL tag is not visible to either KDC rule. Event 41 (adcs_kdc_certificate_sid_mismatch.yml) is the use-side tell for ESC6.
falsepositives: Web server or appliance templates whose owners request SAN entries through certreq -attrib on a CA that deliberately has EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 set. Put those templates in filter_enrollee_subject_templates.

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a zone transfer request received by the Windows DNS server via the Microsoft-Windows-DNSServer/Analytical channel: event 270 (AXFR_REQ_RECV) or 266 (IXFR_REQ_RECV), each carrying the requesting Source address and Zone. author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects PrintNightmare via the PrintService Admin/Operational log: a new printer driver added (316) or a plug-in module load failure (808) that accompanies CVE-2021-1675 / CVE-2021-34527 exploitation.

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects ADCS abuse tooling on the command line: Certify, Certipy and certreq/certutil enrolment patterns. PDF reference: ADCS abuse via Rubeus asktgt /certificate and ntlmrelayx --adcs.

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects ESENT Application log events 325 (database created), 326 (database attached) and 327 (database detached) that name an ntds.dit outside the live NTDS path. ntdsutil IFM, esentutl and offline tooling run on the DC open a copy of the database through the ESE engine, which logs the path of the copy. The DC's own NTDS instance logs the live path, which is filtered.

Backup products that mount a copy of the database for verification

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Impacket GetADUsers.py and GetUserSPNs.py execution from disk or in Windows-converted exe form. PDF reference: "GetADUsers.py -all -dc-ip ..." and "GetUserSPNs.py -request -dc-ip ...".

title: Impacket GetADUsers / GetUserSPNs Reconnaissance

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Certificate Services configuration tampering recorded by the CA in the Security log, by an account that is not an approved PKI administrator. 4882 security permissions for Certificate Services changed (ESC7, granting ManageCA or ManageCertificates), 4885 audit filter changed (turning CA auditing down to blind the other AD CS rules), 4890 certificate manager settings changed, 4891 configuration entry changed, and 4892 a property of Certificate Services changed.

title: Certificate Services Security, Audit Filter or Configuration Changed

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the PowerShell helper functions that Evil-WinRM loads into the remote session and offers in its menu (Invoke-Binary, Dll-Loader, Donut-Loader). The client sends their definitions and the operator's calls to the target, where they run inside wsmprovhost.exe and are recorded by PowerShell script block logging (event 4104). Security research scripts that quote these function names

title: Evil-WinRM Helper Function Names in PowerShell Script Block

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of shadow copies via vssadmin, wmic shadowcopy or diskshadow. Common precursor to NTDS.dit or SAM hive theft. PDF reference: "diskshadow list shadows all" and mklink GLOBALROOT shadow copy access. Paired effect rules are ntds_dit_file_read_4663 (the read out of the shadow copy) and vss_service_idle_shutdown_8224; the shadow_copy_then_ntds_dit_read correlation joins this rule to the 4663 read on the same host.
falsepositives: Authorised backup operations

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects 4794, an attempt to set the Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) administrator password on a Domain Controller. Every DC has a local DSRM administrator whose password is set at promotion and rarely changed. An attacker with DC admin rights sets it to a known value, or syncs it from a domain account whose NTLM hash they hold (ntdsutil "set dsrm password" "sync from domain account"), then combines it with DsrmAdminLogonBehavior 2 for a network logon backdoor that survives domain password resets, or with a DSRM boot for offline access to ntds.dit. Microsoft's guidance is to always monitor 4794 and alert when it occurs.
falsepositives: Planned DSRM password rotation or synchronisation, or DC recovery preparation, by a Tier-0 administrator (ticketed; a recurring sync job should be suppressed by SubjectUserName and Computer)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4794
title: Directory Services Restore Mode Administrator Password Set Attempt

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of .kirbi or .ccache files, or processes calling sekurlsa::tickets /export or Rubeus dump /nowrap. PDF reference: "sekurlsa::tickets / export" and "Rubeus dump /service:krbtgt /nowrap".
falsepositives: Authorised Kerberos tooling such as msktutil or kinit

title: Kerberos Ticket Export to Disk (kirbi/ccache)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the target-side file artefact of remote hive dumping by Impacket secretsdump and CrackMapExec. The tool asks the Remote Registry service to save SAM, SECURITY and SYSTEM to a file with an eight-character random name and a .tmp extension in Windows\Temp (current Impacket) or Windows\System32 (older Impacket and CrackMapExec), pulls it over ADMIN$, then deletes it. The save is performed by the svchost.exe that hosts Remote Registry, so Sysmon 11 records svchost as the writer.
falsepositives: Other svchost-hosted services that write eight-character .tmp names into Windows\Temp (baseline before routing)

title: Remote Registry Hive Save to Random .tmp File (secretsdump Target Artefact)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects command lines of WSUS injection tooling run on a compromised WSUS server to publish a malicious update (WSUSpendu.ps1, wsus-import-cli, PoshWSUS Set-PSWSUSConfig) and the direct SQL path into the SUSDB (sqlcmd against SUSDB / tbUpdate). PDF reference: "WSUSpendu.ps1 # need compromised WSUS server".
falsepositives: WSUS administrators using PoshWSUS for sanctioned configuration (baseline the admin accounts)

title: WSUS Injection Tooling Execution (WSUSpendu / WSUSpect)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center event 41 in the System log of a Domain Controller. The KDC logs it when a certificate presented for PKINIT is otherwise valid but carries a SID in the szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT extension that differs from the SID of the account it mapped to. That is the shape of ESC6 and Certifried (CVE-2022-26923) certificates, whose SAN or dNSHostName names one principal while the CA wrote the requester's SID into the extension. ESC1 is only partly covered. Whether an ESC1 certificate carries a SID extension depends on the template and CA, which KB5014754 does not spell out; one without it maps weakly and can surface as event 39 (adcs_kdc_certificate_weak_mapping.yml) in Compatibility mode, and one that carries the target's SID in the SAN URL tag is a strong mapping and is not expected to produce either event.
falsepositives: A certificate reissued to an account that was deleted and recreated with the same name (new SID, old certificate). Rare; replace the certificate.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center' OR Provider_Name='Kdcsvc') AND EventID=41)
title: KDC Certificate SID Extension Differs from the Mapped Account (KB5014754 Event 41)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects SharpHound and bloodhound-python collection artefacts (process names, ingestor command-line flags, default output filenames). PDF reference: "bloodhound-python -d <domain> -u <user> -p <pwd> -gc <dc> -c all".
falsepositives: Authorised red team or AD assessment activity
Internal pentests run from approved jump hosts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((((Image LIKE '%\\SharpHound.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\bloodhound-python.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\AzureHound.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='SharpHound.exe' OR OriginalFileName='SharpHound.dll')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%CollectionMethod%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%CollectionMethods%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%--collectionmethod%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-BloodHound%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%bloodhound-python%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%SessionLoop%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%BloodHound.zip%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((CommandLine LIKE '% -c all %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -c all,%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -c DCOnly %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -c DCOnly,%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '% -c all' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -c DCOnly' ESCAPE '\')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%\_users.json%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\_computers.json%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((User LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_AD\_ASSESSMENT\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: BloodHound / SharpHound Collection Activity

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a value added to the sIDHistory attribute (5136, Value Added) whose SID is not one of the privileged well-known RIDs that sid_history_injection alerts on at critical. Adding the SID of an ordinary privileged-by-delegation account or group (a server admin group, a service account with DCSync rights) grants its access just as silently. Writers that produce this 5136 are Mimikatz sid::add (after sid::patch) and ADMT-style DsAddSidHistory. DCShadow and forged tickets with ExtraSids do not produce 5136; see dcshadow_replication_rpcserver and the trust-ticket rules.
falsepositives: Genuine cross-domain migration via ADMT, which writes the source-domain SID of each migrated account (ticketed, scheduled, and visible as 4765 too)

title: SID History Value Added to Account (Non-Privileged RID)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects lsass.exe spawning any child process other than Windows Error Reporting. LSASS has almost no legitimate children; a child is the visible side of code running inside LSASS, such as a custom SSP, password filter or injected module that starts a shell. Requires Sysmon EID 1 with parent process information. The Security 4688 equivalent is lsass_anomalous_child_process_4688.

Patch installation events (rare)
Third-party authentication packages that start a helper process (add the exact Image path to filter_wer after review)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects LaZagne execution by image name or by its module command line. The release build carries no PE version resource, so there is no OriginalFileName to key on; a renamed binary run with a renamed command line is not seen by this rule. PDF reference: "lazagne.exe all".

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the operator side of Impacket wmiexec and smbexec on the target. Both tools redirect each command's output to a file at the root of an administrative share and read it back over SMB. wmiexec names the file "__" followed by the Unix timestamp (for example __1731234567.891) on ADMIN$. smbexec uses C$ and names the file __output up to Impacket 0.12.0 and __output_ followed by eight random letters from 0.13.0 (for example __output_KqZtRmWa). Security event 5145 (detailed file share access) records the share and the relative file name whatever the command line looked like.
falsepositives: Unlikely. Requires a file named exactly __output, __output_<8 letters> or __<10-digit number> at the root of an admin share.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND (ShareName LIKE '%\\ADMIN$' ESCAPE '\' OR ShareName LIKE '%\\C$' ESCAPE '\')) AND (RelativeTargetName REGEXP '^__[0-9]{10}(\.[0-9]+)?$' OR RelativeTargetName REGEXP '^__output(_[A-Za-z]{8})?$'))
title: Impacket wmiexec or smbexec Output File Read over Admin Share (5145)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation (5137) of an Active Directory-integrated DNS node, or a write (5136) to the dnsRecord attribute of one, whose name is wpad, isatap or the wildcard *. By default any authenticated user may create child objects in an AD-integrated zone, so Powermad Invoke-DNSUpdate / New-ADIDNSNode, krbrelayx dnstool.py and Inveigh can add these names and send every client that falls back to them to an attacker host. A wildcard record answers every name that does not exist, which replaces LLMNR and NBT-NS poisoning inside AD. Writing dnsRecord on an existing node covers the revival of a tombstoned wpad node.
falsepositives: A documented WPAD record for proxy auto-configuration created by a DNS administrator (add the account to filter_dns_admins)
Legacy ISATAP routers still registered in DNS (rare today)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=5137 AND ObjectClass='dnsNode') OR (EventID=5136 AND ObjectClass='dnsNode' AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='dnsRecord' AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\')) AND ObjectDN REGEXP '(?i)^DC=(wpad|isatap|\*),' AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DNS\_ADMIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: ADIDNS wpad, isatap or Wildcard Record Created via LDAP

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump living-off-the-land technique used to dump LSASS without dropping a tool, plus procdump and the .NET createdump LOLBIN by command line. Catches the comsvcs.dll plus MiniDump invocation, the generic rundll32-against-lsass dump pattern, procdump -ma/-mp against lsass, and createdump against lsass.
falsepositives: Legitimate diagnostic dumps by support staff (rare; correlate with intent)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%comsvcs.dll%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%inidump%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((CommandLine LIKE '%comsvcs.dll%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%full%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% #24%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%,#24%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% 24 %' ESCAPE '\')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%rundll32%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%lsass%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.dmp%' ESCAPE '\') OR (Image LIKE '%\\procdump.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%lsass%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -ma%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -mp%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (Image LIKE '%\\createdump.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%lsass%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: LSASS Memory Dump via LOLBIN or Dump Utility (comsvcs / procdump / createdump)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects certutil -setreg writing the CA policy module EditFlags (ESC6, "certutil -setreg policy\EditFlags +EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2") or the CA InterfaceFlags (ESC11, "certutil -setreg CA\InterfaceFlags -IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST"). Paired effect rule is adcs_ca_config_tamper_registry.yml (Sysmon 13 on the same values), which also catches reg.exe, PowerShell and direct API writes.

rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\certutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='CertUtil.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-setreg%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/setreg%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\EditFlags%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\InterfaceFlags%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% InterfaceFlags%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%"InterfaceFlags%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: certutil Sets CA Policy EditFlags or InterfaceFlags (ESC6, ESC11)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the setup step of targeted AS-REP Roasting. An attacker with write rights over a user (GenericWrite, GenericAll) sets DONT_REQ_PREAUTH (4194304 in userAccountControl), roasts the account, then often clears the flag again. The rule fires on a 4738 (user) or 4742 (computer) account change where the new UAC value has the bit and the old value did not, or where the rendered UserAccountControl change list says "Don't Require Preauth" was enabled. Tooling: PowerView Set-DomainObject -XOR useraccountcontrol, bloodyAD add uac DONT_REQ_PREAUTH, Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth.
falsepositives: Provisioning of a legacy application account that genuinely cannot do pre-authentication (rare, should be ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4738 OR EventID=4742) AND ((NewUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[13579bdfBDF][0-9a-fA-F]{4}$' AND (NOT COALESCE((OldUacValue REGEXP '^0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]*[13579bdfBDF][0-9a-fA-F]{4}$'), 0))) OR (UserAccountControl LIKE '%\%\%2096%' ESCAPE '\' OR UserAccountControl LIKE '%''Don''t Require Preauth'' - Enabled%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Kerberos Pre-Authentication Disabled on an Account (Targeted AS-REP Roasting Setup)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects modification of gPLink on the Domain Controllers OU or domain root, a change to the client-side extension lists of a GPO linked to a sensitive container, or a DACL change on a Group Policy container. These are the GPO abuse paths (SharpGPOAbuse, pyGPOAbuse, PowerView New-GPOImmediateTask) and GPO delegation backdoors. The previous version alerted on every directory change under CN=Policies, including routine versionNumber increments; the condition now requires both the event and the attribute or DACL constraint. PDF reference: "GPO Delegation".
falsepositives: Authorised GPO change windows (populate filter_gpo_admins and correlate with change tickets)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPLink' AND (ObjectDN LIKE '%OU=Domain Controllers%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectDN LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_TIER0\_OU\_DN%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPLink' AND ObjectClass='domainDNS') OR (EventID=5136 AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPCMachineExtensionNames' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPCUserExtensionNames' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='gPCFileSysPath') AND ObjectDN LIKE '%CN=Policies,CN=System%' ESCAPE '\') OR (EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor' AND ObjectClass='groupPolicyContainer') OR ((EventID=5137 OR EventID=5141) AND ObjectClass='groupPolicyContainer')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_GPO\_ADMIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: GPO Link, Extension or Permissions Changed on Sensitive Container

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects dnscmd.exe /config /serverlevelplugindll, the DnsAdmins to Domain Controller escalation path, and the DNS service stop that follows so the plugin DLL is loaded on restart. The registry write itself is covered by the sibling registry_set rule dns_admin_serverlevel_plugin_dll_registry.yml. This rule was split from a mixed-source rule whose registry branch could never match a process_creation event. PDF reference: "dnscmd.exe /config /serverlevelplugindll <\\path\to\dll>".
falsepositives: Documented DNS plugin deployment (vanishingly rare)
DNS service restarts by DNS administrators during maintenance (the restart branch alone is medium confidence)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%serverlevelplugindll%' ESCAPE '\' OR (((Image LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%stop%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%dns%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%dnscache%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Dnscache%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: DnsAdmins ServerLevelPluginDll Set via dnscmd or DNS Service Restart

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects an nTSecurityDescriptor write (5136 Value Added) whose new SDDL contains an allow ACE granting GenericAll (GA), WriteDacl (WD), WriteOwner (WO), or the expanded full-control rights string, or a change of the object owner. These are the edges BloodHound reports as GenericAll, WriteDacl and WriteOwner and the rights aclpwn, dacledit.py and PowerView Add-DomainObjectAcl grant. The previous version matched the words "GenericAll" and "WriteOwner", which never appear in SDDL, and included 5139 (object moved), which is unrelated. The regex keeps two-letter rights codes aligned so that adjacent codes (for example SW followed by DT) are not misread as WD. PDF reference: "Generic All on User / Group / Computer", "WriteOwner on Group", "WriteDACL + WriteOwner".
falsepositives: Documented delegation work by identity administrators (ticketed; add their accounts to a SIEM allowlist, not to this rule)
Exchange and SCCM setup granting rights to their own service groups during installation
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor' AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\') AND (AttributeValue REGEXP '\(A;[^;]*;(?:[A-Z]{2})*(?:GA|WD|WO)(?:[A-Z]{2})*;[^;]*;[^;]*;(?:S-1-5-21-(?:[0-9]+-){3}[0-9]{4,}|DU|DC|DG|AU|WD|AN|BU|BG|IU|NU)\)' OR (AttributeValue LIKE 'O:S-1-5-21-%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((AttributeValue REGEXP '^O:S-1-5-21-[0-9-]+-(500|512|519|518|544)G:'), 0)))))
title: Dangerous ACE Granted or Owner Changed on AD Object (GenericAll / WriteDacl / WriteOwner)

author: 404secnotfound

author: 404secnotfound

author: 404secnotfound
description: Native-log sibling of wmi_persistence_subscription for hosts without Sysmon. Those two classes are how WMI persistence runs a payload; log-only consumers such as NTEventLogEventConsumer are left out.

title: WMI Permanent Event Consumer Binding Registered (WMI-Activity 5861)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Set-MpPreference or Add-MpPreference setting the attack surface reduction rule "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem" (9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2) to Disabled, Audit or NotConfigured (0, 2 or 5), and Remove-MpPreference removing it. title: Defender ASR Rule Block Credential Stealing from LSASS Turned Off with MpPreference

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects successful 4768 TGT requests using RC4 (0x17) with password-style pre-authentication in environments where AES is the default. Indicates Overpass-the-Hash (NTLM -> Kerberos) via Rubeus asktgt /rc4 or Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth. PDF reference: "Rubeus asktgt /user:victim /rc4:<rc4value>".
falsepositives: Legacy clients (Win7 / 2008 R2) and non-Windows Kerberos clients that still default to RC4
Accounts whose msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes or missing AES keys (password never reset since the domain gained AES) force RC4
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4768 AND Status='0x0' AND TicketEncryptionType='0x17' AND (PreAuthType=2 OR PreAuthType=11))
title: Overpass-the-Hash via RC4 TGT Request from User Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects AS-REP Roasting: a successful 4768 TGT request issued without Kerberos pre-authentication (PreAuthType 0) with an RC4 ticket, the encryption type GetNPUsers.py and Rubeus asreproast request by default because it cracks fastest. The AES variant is asrep_roasting_4768_aes and the setup step (pre-authentication being switched off) is asrep_roast_preauth_disabled_set. PDF reference: "python GetNPUsers.py <domain>/ -usersfile <users.txt> -format hashcat".
falsepositives: Legacy service accounts intentionally configured without pre-authentication (inventory them and remove the flag; an allowlist would hide roasting of exactly those accounts)
