title: AS-REP Roasting via Pre-Authentication-Disabled Accounts

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects coerced authentication over the non-EFSR members of the coercion family catalogued by Coercer. Trigger: a remote 5145 access over IPC$ to a named pipe that exposes a coercible RPC interface. Two branches. (1) Pipes with almost no legitimate remote client traffic to a Domain Controller fire on their own: netdfs (MS-DFSNM, DFSCoerce) and FssagentRpc (MS-FSRVP, ShadowCoerce). (2) Pipes that Windows clients open all day (spoolss for MS-RPRN, the printer bug; eventlog for MS-EVEN; MsFteWds for MS-WSP) fire only on an Impacket-style pipe open, AccessMask 0x3 (ReadData and WriteData), the desired access the Impacket SMB client requests for every DCERPC-over-SMB pipe it opens. Branch 2 is therefore coercion (printerbug.py, Coercer) or any other Impacket-based client of those interfaces run from a host that is not an allowlisted admin host; triage decides which. Windows' own RPC client is typically logged opening pipes with 0x12019F. MS-EFSR (efsrpc, and lsarpc, lsass, samr, netlogon with 0x3) is covered only by petitpotam_efsrpc_coercion, so one 5145 raises one alert from this pair. Requires Detailed File Share auditing (5145) on IPC$.
falsepositives: Legitimate DFS management (netdfs) and VSS for SMB file shares backup (FssagentRpc) from known admin or backup hosts (populate filter_admin_hosts)

Impacket-based tooling other than coercion that opens spoolss, eventlog or MsFteWds requests the same 0x3 mask; it is not coercion, but it is still offensive or audit tooling. Confirm coercion by an outbound SMB or HTTP authentication from the target to IpAddress within seconds (exploitation/printer_bug_spooler_coercion.yml, or a 4624 of the target's machine account elsewhere)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND ShareName LIKE '%\\IPC$' ESCAPE '\') AND ((RelativeTargetName='netdfs' OR RelativeTargetName='FssagentRpc') OR ((RelativeTargetName='spoolss' OR RelativeTargetName='eventlog' OR RelativeTargetName='MsFteWds') AND AccessMask='0x3')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::ffff:127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1' OR IpAddress='-') OR (IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_VENDOR\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_VENDOR\_IP' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: Authentication Coercion or Impacket-Style Pipe Open via MS-RPRN / MS-DFSNM / MS-FSRVP / MS-EVEN / MS-WSP Named Pipes

author: 404secnotfound

author: 404secnotfound

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects addition of any principal to a Tier-0 domain group (4728 global, 4732 domain local, 4756 universal) and removal of a member from Protected Users (4729, 4733, 4757). Groups are matched by the group SID suffix in TargetSid as well as by name, so renamed groups and localised OS group names still match. Fixed-RID domain groups. Domain Admins 512, Domain Controllers 516, Cert Publishers 517, Schema Admins 518, Enterprise Admins 519, Group Policy Creator Owners 520, Read-only Domain Controllers 521, Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers 498, Key Admins 526, Enterprise Key Admins 527, Protected Users 525. Builtin groups that exist only on DCs. Account Operators S-1-5-32-548, Server Operators 549, Print Operators 550, and Backup Operators 551. Groups without a fixed RID are matched by name. DnsAdmins, Exchange Windows Permissions and Organization Management. Builtin Administrators and Remote Desktop Users moved to builtin_admin_group_addition, because member servers log the same event for their local groups. PDF reference: "net group 'domain admins' myuser /add /domain".

New CA servers joining Cert Publishers and new DCs joining Domain Controllers during promotion
Exchange setup populating its own groups
Removal from Protected Users of an account that has to use NTLM or delegation (ticketed)

title: Member Added to a Tier-0 Domain Group or Removed from Protected Users

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects changes to domain trust relationships. 4706 a new trust was created, 4707 a trust was removed, 4716 trusted domain information was modified (trust direction, attributes, SID filtering), and 4865, 4866 and 4867 forest trust information entries (top-level names and domain SIDs) added, removed or modified. Attackers add a trust to a domain they control or relax SID filtering on an existing trust so that sIDHistory or ExtraSids in forged tickets are honoured across it. The 4716 that the automatic 30-day trust password rotation logs under ANONYMOUS LOGON is excluded and recorded by trust_account_automatic_password_reset instead.
falsepositives: Planned trust creation, removal or reconfiguration during mergers, divestments and migrations (ticketed, rare)
Trust repair by an administrator (netdom trust /reset), which logs 4716 under the administrator's account
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4706 OR EventID=4707 OR EventID=4716 OR EventID=4865 OR EventID=4866 OR EventID=4867) AND (NOT COALESCE((EventID=4716 AND SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-7' AND SubjectLogonId='0x3e6'), 0)))
title: Domain or Forest Trust Created, Removed or Modified

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a System 7045 service install by a PsExec-family tool. Four independent branches. (1) Sysinternals PsExec, PAExec, CSExec and RemCom by service name or binary name. (2) Impacket psexec.py, which uploads a binary with an eight-letter random name to the ADMIN$ share and installs it as a service with a four-letter random name, so the 7045 shows a service name of four letters and a binary of %systemroot%\<8 letters>.exe. (3) Metasploit psexec with the Native upload target, which uses the same eight-letter binary in %systemroot% with an eight- or sixteen-character random service name. (4) Metasploit psexec with its default Automatic target, which picks the PowerShell target when powershell.exe exists on the target and installs a service whose command is "%COMSPEC% /b /c start /b /min powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -noni ...". The earlier "Impacket" clause (cmd.exe /Q /c ... __output) was in fact the smbexec pattern and now lives only in smbexec_service_command_execution. PDF reference: "psexec.py -hashes ':<hash>' <user>@<ip>".
falsepositives: Sanctioned PsExec use by IT support. 7045 records the target host only, not the source, so tune in the SIEM by joining the 4624 LogonType 3 logged on the same Computer within a few seconds and allowlisting the jump host IpAddress.
A vendor service whose four-letter name and eight-letter binary sit directly in the Windows directory (rare; add the exact service name to a SIEM allowlist)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (EventID=7045 AND ((ServiceName LIKE '%PSEXESVC%' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName LIKE '%PAExec%' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName LIKE '%CSExecSvc%' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName LIKE '%RemComSvc%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ImagePath LIKE '%PSEXESVC.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%\\PAExec-%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%csexecsvc.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImagePath LIKE '%RemComSvc.exe%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ImagePath REGEXP '(?i)^(%systemroot%|c:\\windows)\\[a-z]{8}\.exe$' AND ServiceName REGEXP '^([a-zA-Z]{4}|[a-zA-Z0-9]{8}|[a-zA-Z0-9]{16})$') OR (ImagePath LIKE '%/b /c start /b /min powershell%' ESCAPE '\' AND ImagePath LIKE '%-nop -w hidden -noni%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PsExec-Style Service Install for Remote Code Execution

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a read handle on the registry hive files under \Windows\System32\config or on a Volume Shadow Copy path by a process that is not part of the OS or a known backup agent. CVE-2021-36934 left the hives world-readable via shadow copies; tooling (HiveNightmare, SeriousSAM readers, Mimikatz lsadump::sam /system) opens them directly. Uses Security 4663 (object access) and requires a SACL for Read on the hive files, or Audit File System with a global object access policy. The previous version of this rule used Sysmon file-create telemetry, which never records a read and therefore could not fire.
falsepositives: Backup software reading hives or shadow copies (put its full image path in PLACEHOLDER_BACKUP_AGENT_IMAGE or add full-path list entries)
Vulnerability scanners with credentialed access checking CVE-2021-36934
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4663 AND (ObjectName LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SAM' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SECURITY' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM' ESCAPE '\') AND AccessMask REGEXP '^0x[0-9a-fA-F]*[13579bdfBDF]$') AND (NOT COALESCE(((ProcessName='System' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\smss.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wininit.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\servicing\\TrustedInstaller.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\drvinst.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\poqexec.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessName LIKE '%\\TiWorker.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR ((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessName LIKE '%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\MsSense.exe' ESCAPE '\')) OR (ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbengine.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\VSSVC.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_AGENT\_IMAGE' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: SAM / SECURITY / SYSTEM Hive Read by Non-System Process (HiveNightmare / SeriousSAM)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects ntdsutil run with the "set dsrm password" context, either "sync from domain account <user>" (copies the NTLM hash of a domain account into the local DSRM administrator) or "reset password on server". With the DSRM password known and DsrmAdminLogonBehavior set to 2, an attacker keeps a local administrator logon on the DC that no domain password reset removes.
falsepositives: Planned DSRM password synchronisation from a dedicated domain account, the feature Microsoft documents in KB961320 (suppress by the exact CommandLine and Computer once ticketed)
DC recovery preparation by a Tier-0 administrator (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\ntdsutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='ntdsutil.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%dsrm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sync from domain account%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%reset password on server%' ESCAPE '\')))

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Sysmon image load (EID 7) into lsass.exe of any module that is not validly signed, that is Signed is not true or SignatureStatus is not Valid. Custom security support providers, authentication packages and password filter DLLs are loaded into LSASS at boot or through AddSecurityPackage; attacker builds of these (mimilib, custom SSPs, password-capturing filters) are almost never validly signed, whatever the file is named. Generic catch-all behind the name-based mimikatz_dll_image_load_lsass.
falsepositives: Legacy third-party password filters or authentication packages that ship unsigned (inventory HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa Notification Packages, Authentication Packages and Security Packages first, then filter by exact ImageLoaded path and hash)
Modules whose signature could not be checked at load time, which Sysmon reports with a SignatureStatus other than Valid
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=7 AND (Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((Signed='true' AND SignatureStatus='Valid'), 0))))
title: LSASS Loaded a DLL Without a Valid Signature

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects lsass.exe initiating outbound connections outside the expected authentication ports. Indicator of credential-exfil tooling injected into LSASS or a rogue SSP phoning home. The filter excludes Kerberos, LDAP, DNS and the common federation/RADIUS ports to suppress hybrid-identity false positives. Requires Sysmon EID 3.
falsepositives: ADFS, Azure AD / Entra hybrid auth and RADIUS/NPS on non-standard ports (extend filter)
RPC to a domain controller not yet listed in filter_domain_controllers (Netlogon secure channel, replication)
CRL and OCSP retrieval over port 80 during smart card or PKINIT certificate validation (add the exact CRL host IPs)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND Initiated='true') AND (NOT COALESCE(((DestinationPort=88 OR DestinationPort=389 OR DestinationPort=636 OR DestinationPort=3268 OR DestinationPort=3269 OR DestinationPort=53 OR DestinationPort=443 OR DestinationPort=1812 OR DestinationPort=1813 OR DestinationPort=49443) OR (DestinationIp LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR DestinationIp LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_IP' ESCAPE '\') OR (DestinationIp='127.0.0.1' OR DestinationIp='::1')), 0))))
title: LSASS Initiating Anomalous Outbound Network Connection

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects writes to msDS-KeyCredentialLink on a user or computer object, the Shadow Credentials technique (Whisker / pyWhisker / Certipy shadow) that adds an attacker-controlled key credential for certificate-based auth and PKINIT. The use step (a PKINIT TGT for the same account) is joined by shadow_credentials_pkinit_use_correlation, and a PKINIT logon with a certificate not issued by the enterprise CA is pkinit_non_enterprise_ca_issuer.
falsepositives: Windows Hello for Business and Azure AD device registration write this attribute legitimately (populate filter_aad)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-KeyCredentialLink') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_AAD\_OR\_DEVICE\_REG\_ACCOUNT%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Shadow Credentials via msDS-KeyCredentialLink Write

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Juicy / Lovely / Rogue / God / Sweet Potato and PrintSpoofer execution: the tool binary by name, or a service identity (IIS APPPOOL\, NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE or LOCAL SERVICE) as the parent of cmd.exe or powershell.exe running as SYSTEM, which is the result of abusing SeImpersonatePrivilege. Effect rules that do not depend on the command line are seimpersonate_potato_named_pipe.yml (Sysmon 17 nested pipe path) and seimpersonate_service_to_system_4688.yml (Security 4688 creator and target identities). PDF reference: "Juicy Potato / Lovely Potato / RoguePotato / PrintSpoofer".
falsepositives: Service self-elevation paths in custom apps (rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\PrintSpoofer.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\PrintSpoofer64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\JuicyPotato.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\RoguePotato.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\GodPotato.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\SweetPotato.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\LovelyPotato.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (((ParentUser LIKE '%IIS APPPOOL%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentUser LIKE '%NETWORK SERVICE%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentUser LIKE '%LOCAL SERVICE%' ESCAPE '\') AND User LIKE '%SYSTEM%' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((ParentImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: SeImpersonate Potato / PrintSpoofer Privilege Escalation

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Security 4697 (a service was installed in the system) where the service binary path points to a printer driver staging directory or a temp path, a follow-on of PrintNightmare DLL execution. Sibling of the System 7045 rule; 4697 needs Audit Security System Extension and carries the installing account, which 7045 does not.
falsepositives: Legitimate driver-bundled services (rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4697 AND (ServiceFileName LIKE '%\\spool\\drivers\\x64\\3\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceFileName LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: PrintNightmare Service Install with Driver/Temp Binary Path (Security 4697)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Security 5145 on the SYSVOL or NETLOGON share where the requested access includes a write right (WriteData or AddFile, AppendData or AddSubdirectory, DELETE, WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER) by an account outside the Group Policy administrator allowlist. Writing a logon script, a ScheduledTasks.xml immediate task (SharpGPOAbuse, pyGPOAbuse), a Registry.pol or a GptTmpl.inf into a GPO folder, or replacing a script in NETLOGON, executes attacker code on every computer or user the GPO or script applies to. Domain Controllers replicate SYSVOL with DFSR, which does not go through the share and does not produce 5145, so legitimate writes come only from administrators editing policy.
falsepositives: Administrators outside the allowlist maintaining logon scripts in NETLOGON (add them to filter_gpo_admins)

Domain Admins browsing SYSVOL in Explorer, where a MAXIMUM_ALLOWED open lists every granted right including write rights (review RelativeTargetName; a directory listing on the share root is the usual shape)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND (ShareName LIKE '%\\SYSVOL' ESCAPE '\' OR ShareName LIKE '%\\NETLOGON' ESCAPE '\') AND (AccessList LIKE '%\%\%4417%' ESCAPE '\' OR AccessList LIKE '%\%\%4418%' ESCAPE '\' OR AccessList LIKE '%\%\%1537%' ESCAPE '\' OR AccessList LIKE '%\%\%1539%' ESCAPE '\' OR AccessList LIKE '%\%\%1540%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_GPO\_ADMIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Write Access to SYSVOL or NETLOGON by a Non-GPO-Admin Account

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects modification of an existing Windows service's binary path (sc config binPath=) so the service launches a command interpreter or script host on next start. Distinct from service creation (7045): no new service is registered, so the PsExec/smbexec service-install rules do not fire. Used for privilege escalation and persistence by repointing a benign service at attacker code.
falsepositives: Documented service reconfiguration by administrators or installers (baseline the service names and admin hosts that legitimately do this)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (Image LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%config%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%binpath%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%cmd%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.bat%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%rundll32%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%mshta%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cscript%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%wscript%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Existing Service Binary Path Modified to Command Interpreter

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Impacket wmiexec.py: cmd.exe spawned by WmiPrvSE.exe with output redirected to \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__<timestamp>. Runs with -nooutput keep cmd.exe /Q /c but drop the redirect and are left to the low sibling wmiprvse_shell_spawn_user_context. Runs with -silentcommand start the operator's binary directly under WmiPrvSE with no cmd.exe and are not covered by any sibling. PDF reference: "wmiexec.py -hashes ':<hash>' <user>@<ip>".
falsepositives: Custom monitoring solutions invoking WMI command execution (rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (ParentImage LIKE '%\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND Image LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/Q%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%1>%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\ADMIN$\\\_\_%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Impacket WMIExec Remote Command Pattern

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects copying or saving of SAM, SECURITY or SYSTEM registry hives via reg.exe save, esentutl, vssadmin shadow copy followed by hive copy, or secretsdump on a workstation. PDF reference: "--sam / --lsa / --ntds".
falsepositives: Backup software using esentutl /y (filter by parent process)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%save HKLM\\SAM%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%save HKLM\\SECURITY%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%save HKLM\\SYSTEM%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%save hklm\\sam%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%save hklm\\security%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%save hklm\\system%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((Image LIKE '%\\esentutl.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/y%' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%/vss%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ntds.dit%' ESCAPE '\') OR CommandLine REGEXP '(?i)\\config\\(sam|security|system)([^a-z0-9_]|$)')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '% --sam%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% --lsa%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% --ntds%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%secretsdump%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%lsassy%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: SAM / SECURITY / SYSTEM Hive Copy or Save

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of PSEXESVC, paexec, csexec, RemCom and Impacket named pipes. Impacket psexec.py deploys RemComSvc, whose pipes are \RemCom_communicaton (sic), \RemCom_stdin, \RemCom_stdout and \RemCom_stderr. Sysmon records PipeName without the \\.\pipe\ prefix, so the previous \\.\pipe\impacket- pattern could not match. Requires Sysmon EID 17 (PipeCreated) or EID 18 (PipeConnected). The pipe_created log source covers both: the service creates the pipe (17) and the remote client's connection over SMB is logged as a connect to the same PipeName (18), so either event alone raises the alert. The generic stdin/stdout/stderr pipes were removed because they match every PowerShell remoting and WinRM session.
falsepositives: Sanctioned PsExec administration (tune by source host)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND ((EventID=17 OR EventID=18) AND ((PipeName LIKE '%\\PSEXESVC%' ESCAPE '\' OR PipeName LIKE '%\\paexec%' ESCAPE '\' OR PipeName LIKE '%\\csexec%' ESCAPE '\' OR PipeName LIKE '%\\remcom%' ESCAPE '\') OR (PipeName LIKE '\\impacket%' ESCAPE '\' OR PipeName LIKE '\\RemCom\_%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PsExec / Impacket Named Pipe Creation

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects any audited access (4662) to the decoy user object or the decoy group object in Active Directory, for any property and any access type. A SACL on each decoy audits reads by Everyone, so LDAP reconnaissance that pulls the object's attributes or security descriptor is logged: BloodHound and SharpHound collection, PowerView, ADExplorer snapshots, ldapsearch and ldapdomaindump sweeps. Writes to the decoys are logged by the same SACL if it also audits writes.
falsepositives: Administrators browsing the decoy's OU in Active Directory Users and Computers, ADAC or PowerShell, which reads every child object. Place the decoys in an OU administrators have no routine reason to open. This is why the rule ships at high rather than critical.

Identity governance, AD backup and auditing products that read every object over LDAP on a schedule. Baseline for two weeks before this rule pages, then add each service account that reads the decoys on a schedule to the PLACEHOLDER_HONEY_SANCTIONED_READER01 to 03 list (matched together with PLACEHOLDER_INTERNAL_DOMAIN_NETBIOS). An attacker who controls a listed account is then blind to this rule.
Authorised AD assessments (PingCastle, Purple Knight, BloodHound run by the security team). Confirm the requester with the assessment lead.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND ObjectServer='DS') AND ((ObjectName LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_GUID\_USER01%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_GUID\_GROUP01%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ObjectName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_DN\_USER01' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_DN\_GROUP01' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_SANCTIONED\_READER01' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_SANCTIONED\_READER02' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_SANCTIONED\_READER03' ESCAPE '\') AND SubjectDomainName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_INTERNAL\_DOMAIN\_NETBIOS' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Honeytoken Directory Object Accessed (4662)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a service ImagePath registry value being written with a command interpreter or script host in it. Whatever tool changes or creates a service (sc.exe config binPath=, sc create, PowerShell Set-Service or New-Service, the SCM RPC interface used by Impacket and SharpSCM, or a direct registry edit), the value ends up under HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\ImagePath, so this is the effect-side pair of the command-line rule service_binpath_modification.
falsepositives: Vendor services that wrap their executable in a batch file or cmd.exe (inventory them and allowlist the exact TargetObject in the SIEM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\ImagePath' ESCAPE '\') AND (Details LIKE '%cmd.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%cmd /c%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%\%COMSPEC\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%pwsh%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%mshta%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%rundll32%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%wscript%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%cscript%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%.bat%' ESCAPE '\' OR Details LIKE '%.ps1%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Service ImagePath Set to a Command Interpreter or Script Host (Registry)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects bcdedit configuring the next boot into Directory Services Restore Mode (safeboot dsrepair). On a Domain Controller, DSRM starts Windows with AD DS offline and lets the local DSRM administrator log on, which an attacker uses to copy ntds.dit offline or to plant persistence while the directory, its auditing and most EDR hooks are not running. The option is only meaningful on a DC, so the rule does not restrict the host.
falsepositives: Documented AD forest recovery or authoritative restore by a Tier-0 administrator (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (((Image LIKE '%\\bcdedit.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='bcdedit.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%safeboot%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%dsrepair%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine REGEXP '(?i)\s[/-]deletevalue\s'), 0))))
title: Boot Configuration Set to Directory Services Repair Mode (bcdedit safeboot dsrepair)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting performed without a dedicated tool, using PowerView/PowerSploit functions or the native .NET KerberosRequestorSecurityToken class to request service tickets from a domain-joined foothold. Catches the on-host command behaviour; the encryption anomaly itself is caught by kerberoasting_4769_rc4 and asrep_roasting_4768_preauth. Keyed on durable function and class names, not a binary, so a rename does not defeat it.
falsepositives: Sanctioned purple-team or detection-validation activity from known hosts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=1 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-Kerberoast%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Request-SPNTicket%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%KerberosRequestorSecurityToken%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-ASREPRoast%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Get-DomainSPNTicket%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Toolless Kerberoasting / AS-REP Roasting via PowerShell

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects the two CA registry changes that open ESC6 and ESC11 on an Enterprise CA. ESC6. The policy module EditFlags value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CertSvc\Configuration\<CA>\PolicyModules\<module>\EditFlags is written with EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 (0x00040000) set, which makes the CA honour a SAN supplied as a request attribute for any template. ESC11. Configuration\<CA>\InterfaceFlags is written with IF_ENFORCEENCRYPTICERTREQUEST (0x00000200) clear, which lets ICertPassage (MS-ICPR) RPC requests be relayed over NTLM. The change takes effect at the next CertSvc restart.
falsepositives: A PKI administrator deliberately enabling EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 for a legacy SAN workflow. That is itself an ESC6 exposure; ticket and review it.
Rewrites of the value with the bit unchanged (for example a configuration management run that rewrites every CA value) on a CA already exposed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Services\\CertSvc\\Configuration\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\PolicyModules\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\EditFlags' ESCAPE '\') AND Details REGEXP 'DWORD \(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{3}[4-7c-fC-F][0-9a-fA-F]{4}\)') OR ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Services\\CertSvc\\Configuration\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\InterfaceFlags' ESCAPE '\') AND Details REGEXP 'DWORD \(0x[0-9a-fA-F]{5}[014589cdCD][0-9a-fA-F]{2}\)')))
title: CA Policy EditFlags SAN Attribute Enabled or Request Encryption Disabled (ESC6, ESC11)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects coercion via MS-RPRN spooler API. Trigger on outbound SMB connection from spoolsv.exe to any non-print-server host. PDF reference: "printerbug.py '<domain>/<user>:<pwd>'@<Printer> <RESPONDERIP>". Operators should populate a print-server allowlist in the filter section.
falsepositives: Print server to print server replication (extend filter)
Cluster heartbeat traffic
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND ((Image LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\spoolsv.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND Initiated='true' AND (DestinationPort=445 OR DestinationPort=139)) AND (NOT COALESCE((DestinationIp='127.0.0.1' OR DestinationIp='::1'), 0))))
title: Printer Bug Spooler Coercion (RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects reads of the gMSA managed-password blob via 4662 on the msDS-ManagedPassword attribute. Abused by GoldenGMSA and the dMSA pivot to recover service-account credentials. Filtering uses a POSITIVE allowlist of the hosts authorised to retrieve each gMSA password, because gMSA consumers are themselves machine accounts; a blanket machine-account filter would let a compromised machine account read another gMSA undetected.
falsepositives: Authorised gMSA-consuming hosts (populate filter_authorised_gmsa_hosts with the PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword set for each gMSA)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND Properties LIKE '%e362ed86-b728-0842-b27d-2dea7a9df218%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_GMSA\_HOST01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_GMSA\_HOST02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: gMSA msDS-ManagedPassword Attribute Read (GoldenGMSA)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects coerced NTLM authentication via MS-EFSR, the interface PetitPotam uses to force a Domain Controller to authenticate to an attacker host. Triggers on a 5145 access over IPC$ to the efsrpc pipe, which has almost no legitimate remote client traffic, or on an Impacket-style pipe open of the lsarpc, lsass, samr or netlogon pipes that also expose MS-EFSR: AccessMask 0x3 (ReadData and WriteData), the desired access the Impacket SMB client requests for every DCERPC-over-SMB pipe it opens. That second branch is therefore PetitPotam.py or Coercer, or Impacket-based enumeration of LSA and SAMR (lookupsid, samrdump, NetExec user, RID-brute and password-policy queries, BloodHound.py local group collection) run from a host that is not an allowlisted admin host. Both are offensive or audit tooling; triage decides which. Windows' own RPC client is typically logged opening these pipes with 0x12019F, so ordinary domain traffic to lsarpc and samr does not match. The other coercion interfaces (DFSCoerce, ShadowCoerce, printer bug, MS-EVEN, MS-WSP) are covered only by coercion_multi_vector_named_pipes, so one 5145 raises one alert from this pair. PDF reference: "PetitPotam.py -d <domain> <listener_ip> <target_ip>".
falsepositives: Backup and EFS management agents (Veeam, CommVault, Rubrik) touching efsrpc or lsarpc from known hosts (populate filter_backup_hosts)

Impacket-based enumeration (lookupsid, samrdump, NetExec --users, --rid-brute or --pass-pol, BloodHound.py) opens lsarpc and samr with the same 0x3 mask; it is not coercion, but it is still offensive tooling. Confirm coercion by an outbound SMB or HTTP authentication from the target to IpAddress within seconds (exploitation/printer_bug_spooler_coercion.yml, or a 4624 of the target's machine account elsewhere)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5145 AND ShareName LIKE '%\\IPC$' ESCAPE '\') AND (RelativeTargetName='efsrpc' OR ((RelativeTargetName='lsarpc' OR RelativeTargetName='lsass' OR RelativeTargetName='samr' OR RelativeTargetName='netlogon') AND AccessMask='0x3')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((IpAddress='127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::ffff:127.0.0.1' OR IpAddress='::1' OR IpAddress='-') OR (IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_VENDOR\_IP' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE '::ffff:PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_VENDOR\_IP' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: PetitPotam MS-EFSR Coercion or Impacket-Style LSA / SAMR Pipe Open

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Security event 4688 (version 2) where the creator subject is a service identity (LOCAL SERVICE S-1-5-19, NETWORK SERVICE S-1-5-20, an IIS application pool S-1-5-82-*, or a virtual service account S-1-5-80-* such as NT SERVICE\MSSQLSERVER) and the target subject of the new process is LocalSystem (S-1-5-18) at System integrity (MandatoryLabel S-1-16-16384). This is the observable result of the Potato family and PrintSpoofer, which turn SeImpersonatePrivilege held by a service into a SYSTEM token and call CreateProcessWithTokenW or CreateProcessAsUser. It is the 4688 tier equivalent of the Sysmon branch in seimpersonate_potato_printspoofer.yml and does not depend on the tool name, but it sees only the creation shape in which the service identity is the recorded creator (see the note for the CreateProcessWithTokenW blind spot).
falsepositives: Services that legitimately hold a SYSTEM token and spawn helpers (rare; baseline ParentProcessName per host before routing)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4688 AND TargetUserSid='S-1-5-18' AND MandatoryLabel='S-1-16-16384') AND ((SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-19' OR SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-20') OR (SubjectUserSid LIKE 'S-1-5-82-%' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserSid LIKE 'S-1-5-80-%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Service Identity Creating a SYSTEM Process (4688 Token Impersonation)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a 4624 LogonType 3 NTLM logon where KeyLength is 0, meaning no session key was negotiated. Relayed authentication (ntlmrelayx to LDAP, SMB, HTTP or AD CS) and Linux-origin Pass-the-Hash (xfreerdp /pth, impacket -hashes, nxc) present this way on the target, while the WorkstationName carries the victim's hostname and the IpAddress is the attacker's. Machine accounts are in scope, because a coerced computer account relayed to a member server is the most common relay outcome. Sigma cannot compare WorkstationName to the reverse DNS of IpAddress; compute that mismatch in the SIEM as the high-fidelity filter. This rule consolidates three earlier rules (ntlmrelayx_ldap_relay, pth_linux_xfreerdp_or_relay, ntlm_relay_workstation_mismatch) that keyed on the same event with different severities. The NTLMv1 branch moved to ntlmv1_authentication_logon. PDF reference: "ntlmrelayx.py -t ldap://<dc>" and "xfreerdp /u:<user> /d:<domain> /pth:<hash> /v:<ip>".
falsepositives: Legacy application servers and appliances that negotiate NTLM without a session key (populate filter_known_app_tier)
VPN and NAT paths where source IP legitimately differs from WorkstationName (handle in the SIEM mismatch logic)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND LogonType=3 AND AuthenticationPackageName='NTLM' AND KeyLength=0) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName='ANONYMOUS LOGON' OR IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_APP\_TIER\_HOST' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: NTLM Network Logon Without Session Key (Relay or Linux Pass-the-Hash Candidate)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a .p12 or .pfx file created on the Certification Authority host by certutil.exe, mmc.exe (the Certification Authority console backup wizard and the Certificates snap-in export wizard) or certsrv.exe, outside the sanctioned CA backup location. certutil -backupKey writes the CA certificate and private key as a PFX file into the backup directory, and certutil -exportPFX writes any certificate with its private key. On the CA either is the CA key or a machine key leaving the store, the material behind a Golden Certificate.
falsepositives: A PKI administrator exporting a certificate with certutil -exportPFX or the console for a documented migration
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND ((Computer LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_SERVER\_FQDN' ESCAPE '\' AND (Image LIKE '%\\certutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\mmc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Image LIKE '%\\certsrv.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (TargetFilename LIKE '%.p12' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%.pfx' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetFilename LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_CA\_BACKUP\_PATH%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: PKCS#12 Key File Written on the CA by certutil or the CA Console

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects deletion of the RunAsPPL value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa. Microsoft documents deleting the value, as well as setting it to 0, as a way to disable added LSA protection, which takes effect at the next boot and lets an unprotected process read LSASS memory again.
falsepositives: Troubleshooting an incompatible LSA plug-in (ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND ((EventID=12 AND (EventType='DeleteKey' OR EventType='DeleteValue')) AND (EventType='DeleteValue' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\Lsa\\RunAsPPL' ESCAPE '\'))
title: LSA Protection RunAsPPL Registry Value Deleted

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects image loads of credential-dumping support DLLs (Mimikatz family) into lsass.exe. High-fidelity signal that survives binary rename. Requires Sysmon EID 7. Only loadable image modules are listed; the kiwissp.log file artefact is covered by the file_event rule mimikatz_driver_or_ssp_dll_drop.yml.
falsepositives: Unlikely
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=7 AND ((Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\mimilib.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\mimikatz.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\kiwissp.dll' ESCAPE '\')) OR (Image LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (OriginalFileName='mimilib.dll' OR OriginalFileName='mimidrv.sys' OR OriginalFileName='kiwissp.dll'))))
title: Suspicious DLL Loaded into LSASS (Mimikatz / Credential Dump Tooling)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DCShadow: a computer that is not a legitimate Domain Controller registers the DRS replication SPN (E3514235-4B06-11D1-AB04-00C04FC2DCD2) or a GC/ SPN on itself (4742), creates an nTDSDSA or server object under the Sites container in the Configuration partition (5137), or triggers replica source naming-context events (4928/4929). The 4742 branch excludes the real DC machine accounts via the same positive allowlist the DCSync rule uses, so genuine DC promotions and GC enablement do not fire.
falsepositives: Genuine DC promotion (rare, must be tracked; add the new DC to the allowlist afterwards)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4742 AND (ServicePrincipalNames LIKE '%GC/%' ESCAPE '\' OR ServicePrincipalNames LIKE '%E3514235-4B06-11D1-AB04-00C04FC2DCD2%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR (EventID=5137 AND (ObjectClass='nTDSDSA' OR ObjectClass='server') AND ObjectDN LIKE '%CN=Sites,CN=Configuration%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((EventID=4928 OR EventID=4929) AND (NOT COALESCE((SourceAddr LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01\_DSA\_GUID.%' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceAddr LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02\_DSA\_GUID.%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: DCShadow Indicators (Replication from Non-DC SPN Registration)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of files matching LSASS minidump artefacts: lsass.dmp, lsass.zip, debug.dmp, *.dmp under temp paths. PDF reference: "procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp".
falsepositives: WER crash dumps on actual lsass faults (rare, investigate root cause)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND ((TargetFilename LIKE '%\\lsass%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetFilename LIKE '%.dmp%' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetFilename LIKE '%\\lsass.dmp' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\lsass.bin' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\lsass\_dump.dmp' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\lsass.zip' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\debug.dmp' ESCAPE '\')))
title: LSASS Minidump File Creation on Disk

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects activity against a decoy computer account that has no machine behind it. Three branches. (1) An authentication as the decoy computer (4768, 4771, 4776, 4624, 4625, 4648), which needs its password or key, for example a pre-Windows 2000 computer password guessed by pre2k tooling. (2) A service ticket request to the decoy computer (4769 ServiceName), the last leg of a resource-based constrained delegation (S4U2proxy) or a silver-ticket preparation against it. (3) A directory write of msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity (RBCD) or msDS-KeyCredentialLink (Shadow Credentials) on the decoy computer object (5136), the takeover step that tools such as rbcd.py, KrbRelayUp, Whisker and Certipy shadow perform.
falsepositives: Inventory and vulnerability scanners that resolve the decoy's host name and connect to it with Kerberos, which logs a 4769 for the decoy. Do not publish a DNS record for the decoy, or point it at an address where nothing listens, and exclude the decoy from scanner scope.
An administrator clearing or setting the RBCD or KeyCredentialLink attribute on the decoy during maintenance. Agree a change window and confirm SubjectUserName.
The bootstrap authentication an administrator may perform when creating the decoy. Do it before substituting the placeholders.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4768 OR EventID=4771 OR EventID=4776 OR EventID=4624 OR EventID=4625 OR EventID=4648) AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_COMPUTER01$' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_COMPUTER01$@%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (EventID=4769 AND ServiceName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_COMPUTER01$' ESCAPE '\') OR (EventID=5136 AND ObjectDN LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_DN\_COMPUTER01' ESCAPE '\' AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-KeyCredentialLink')))
title: Honeytoken Computer Account Authentication, Ticket Request or Takeover Write

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Kerberos service ticket request (4769) for the decoy service account, a user account that carries a believable SPN but runs no service. No client has a reason to ask for a ticket to it, so a request means someone enumerated SPNs and requested tickets to crack offline (Kerberoasting with Rubeus, Impacket GetUserSPNs -request, NetExec and similar). The rule is encryption-agnostic, so AES-only roasting that evades the RC4 rule is caught.
falsepositives: Vulnerability scanners and AD assessment tools that enumerate SPNs and request a ticket for each one to test crackability. Tools that only read the SPN over LDAP do not log 4769. Tell the assessment team the decoy exists or exclude it from their scope, and confirm the requester and source address before closing.

A client that resolves the decoy SPN's host name and connects to it. Point the SPN at a host name that does not exist or at an address where nothing listens, and do not reuse a decommissioned server name that old clients may still try.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4769 OR EventID=4768) AND (ServiceName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_KERBEROAST\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\' OR ServiceName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_KERBEROAST\_ACCOUNT@%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Honeytoken SPN Service Ticket Requested (Kerberoast Decoy)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects CreateRemoteThread into lsass.exe, winlogon.exe, services.exe, csrss.exe or smss.exe. Requires Sysmon EID 8.
falsepositives: EDR injection for telemetry (add the agent's full SourceImage path to filter_legit)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=8 AND ((TargetImage LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetImage LIKE '%\\winlogon.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetImage LIKE '%\\services.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetImage LIKE '%\\csrss.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetImage LIKE '%\\smss.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\MsSense.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\CrowdStrike\\CSFalconService.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: CreateRemoteThread Injection into Sensitive Process

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects network share access (5145) to the Group Policy Preferences folder of a decoy GPO, where a planted Groups.xml carries a cpassword for a decoy account. The decoy GPO is not linked to any OU, so no Group Policy client ever reads it. Access means someone is spidering SYSVOL for GPP passwords (Get-GPPPassword, NetExec gpp_password, Snaffler, findstr /S cpassword over the share). If the attacker then decrypts the cpassword and tries it, honey_user_authentication fires on the decoy account.
falsepositives: Scheduled readers of SYSVOL over SMB such as a nightly Backup-GPO -All job, GPO change-management tools, and PingCastle or Purple Knight searching for cpassword. Scope them away from the decoy GPO or close their alerts by source address and schedule.

An administrator opening the Settings report of the decoy GPO in the Group Policy Management Console, which reads the preference files over SYSVOL. Name the decoy GPO so administrators leave it alone and agree who maintains it.
Backup, file-integrity or DLP products that crawl SYSVOL over SMB. Most back up SYSVOL locally through VSS, which logs no 5145; confirm the account and schedule before closing.
A GPO accidentally linked to an OU, after which every computer in scope reads it at each refresh. Keep the decoy GPO unlinked.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=5145 AND (RelativeTargetName LIKE '%PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_GPO\_GUID%' ESCAPE '\' AND RelativeTargetName LIKE '%\\Preferences\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Honeytoken GPP Preference File Accessed in Decoy GPO

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters\ ServerLevelPluginDll. The DNS service loads this DLL as SYSTEM on a Domain Controller at next start, which is the DnsAdmins to Domain Admin escalation. Any value here is anomalous in almost every estate; a UNC path is the attacker default. Requires Sysmon EID 13 or equivalent registry auditing on DNS servers.
falsepositives: Documented DNS plugin deployment (vanishingly rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Services\\DNS\\Parameters\\ServerLevelPluginDll' ESCAPE '\')
title: DNS Server ServerLevelPluginDll Registry Value Set

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects any connection to, or file access within, a decoy network share that no user or application is told about (5140 share accessed, 5145 share object access check), with any access mask and whether access was granted or denied. The share has a tempting name and a few plausible decoy files. Access means someone is crawling shares for data or credentials (Snaffler, NetExec spider_plus, PowerView Find-InterestingDomainShareFile, manual browsing after net view).
falsepositives: Authenticated vulnerability scanners that connect to every share to test its permissions, and DLP, eDiscovery or data-classification crawlers. Exclude the decoy share from their scope at deployment and confirm the account and source address before closing.
Backup agents that back up shares over SMB from a remote server. Back the decoy up locally or not at all.
Share enumeration alone (net view, NetShareEnum over the srvsvc pipe) does not connect to the share and does not fire this rule.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5140 OR EventID=5145) AND ShareName LIKE '%\\PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_SHARE' ESCAPE '\')
title: Honeytoken File Share Accessed

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects 4742 events in which the computer account of a Domain Controller is changed by ANONYMOUS LOGON. Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) exploits reset the DC account password over an unauthenticated Netlogon session, which the DC logs with subject ANONYMOUS LOGON (S-1-5-7, logon ID 0x3e6). Strong corroborating signal alongside Netlogon 5827-5831.
falsepositives: Unlikely once the DC list is complete. Populate TargetUserName with every DC machine account of the domain.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4742 AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\')) AND (SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-7' OR SubjectUserName='ANONYMOUS LOGON'))
title: Domain Controller Computer Account Password Set by Anonymous

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects spoolsv.exe loading a DLL from a non-system path, a strong PrintNightmare signal. Requires Sysmon EID 7 (image_load).
falsepositives: Third-party printer drivers staged in non-standard paths (rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=7 AND (Image LIKE '%\\spoolsv.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\spool\\drivers\\x64\\3\\new\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ((ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ImageLoaded LIKE '%\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((ImageLoaded LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))))
title: PrintNightmare Spooler Loading DLL from Anomalous Path

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects DCSync: a principal exercising the DS-Replication-Get-Changes or DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All control access right on the domain naming context (4662, AccessMask 0x100 Control Access). Filtering uses a positive allowlist of the real Domain Controller machine accounts and the directory-sync service account, so DCSync run under SYSTEM or a compromised machine account on a Tier-0 host is NOT suppressed. Events that carry only DS-Replication-Get-Changes-In-Filtered-Set are handled by the medium sibling dcsync_filtered_set_replication. PDF reference: "lsadump::dcsync /domain:htb.local /user:krbtgt".
falsepositives: Legitimate DC-to-DC replication and directory sync. Populate filter_known_replication_principals with every DC machine account in the forest, all domains (Global Catalogs and DCs of other domains replicate this domain's partial naming context), and the sync service account.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4662 AND AccessMask='0x100' AND (Properties LIKE '%1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2%' ESCAPE '\' OR Properties LIKE '%1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2%' ESCAPE '\')) AND ((ObjectType LIKE '%19195a5b-6da0-11d0-afd3-00c04fd930c9%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectType LIKE '%domainDNS%' ESCAPE '\') OR ObjectType IS NULL) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC01$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DC02$' ESCAPE '\' OR SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_MSOL\_OR\_ADSYNC\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: DCSync via DRSUAPI Replication from Non-DC

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects ACL writes (5136 nTSecurityDescriptor) on high-value AD objects: AdminSDHolder, the Domain Controllers OU and krbtgt. Used by aclpwn and PowerView Add-DomainObjectAcl. Domain-root DACL changes are caught by the PrivExchange rule (objectClass domainDNS). PDF reference: "AD acl abuse / aclpwn.py".
falsepositives: Genuine delegation changes (must be ticketed and rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor' AND (ObjectDN LIKE '%CN=AdminSDHolder%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectDN LIKE '%OU=Domain Controllers%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectDN LIKE '%CN=krbtgt%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: DACL Modified on Privileged AD Object (AdminSDHolder / DC / krbtgt)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects use of the MSOL_ / ADSync directory-sync account from any host other than the sanctioned Entra Connect server. This account holds DCSync rights, so its use elsewhere is a dominant 2025-2026 cloud-to-on-prem pivot.
falsepositives: The Entra Connect server itself (populate filter_known_sync_host with its hostname and filter_known_sync_ip with its address; Kerberos network logons often carry "-" as WorkstationName and only the IP)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4624 AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'MSOL\_%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'ADSync%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'AAD\_%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((WorkstationName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_ENTRA\_CONNECT\_HOST' ESCAPE '\' OR IpAddress LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_ENTRA\_CONNECT\_IP' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Entra Connect / Cloud Sync Account Used from Unexpected Host

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects access to LSASS with Mimikatz / procdump / nanodump style GrantedAccess values (canonical Mimikatz signatures 0x1010, 0x1410, 0x1438, 0x143a), PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS (0x1fffff) from any process other than the path-pinned core system processes (whatever the call stack), and a CallTrace through dbgcore, dbghelp or comsvcs that betrays MiniDumpWriteDump. The EDR allowlist is pinned to install paths, so a binary renamed MsMpEng.exe in a user folder is no longer exempt. PDF reference: "procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp".
falsepositives: EDR, AV or inventory agents installed outside the pinned paths (add their exact install path to filter_legit)
Sysinternals Process Explorer when run as admin (rare on servers)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=10 AND (TargetImage LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ((GrantedAccess='0x1010' OR GrantedAccess='0x1410' OR GrantedAccess='0x1438' OR GrantedAccess='0x143a' OR GrantedAccess='0x1438a' OR GrantedAccess='0x1f0fff' OR GrantedAccess='0x101010') OR (GrantedAccess='0x1fffff' AND (NOT COALESCE((SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\csrss.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wininit.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\services.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsm.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR (CallTrace LIKE '%dbgcore.dll%' ESCAPE '\' OR CallTrace LIKE '%dbghelp.dll%' ESCAPE '\' OR CallTrace LIKE '%comsvcs.dll%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\MpCmdRun.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\%\\MpCmdRun.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\MsSense.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\SenseIR.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Tanium\\Tanium Client\\TaniumClient.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Tanium\\Tanium Client\\TaniumClient.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\CrowdStrike\\CSFalconService.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\SentinelOne\\Sentinel Agent %\\SentinelAgent.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR SourceImage LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\CarbonBlack\\cb.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS for Credential Dumping

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects web shell files written into Exchange front-end directories, a hallmark of post-ProxyLogon/ProxyShell exploitation. Requires Sysmon EID 11 (file_event). No process filter is applied because the exploited Exchange worker (w3wp.exe / UMWorkerProcess) is itself the writer during abuse.
falsepositives: Exchange cumulative-update file writes (rare, correlate with patch window)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND ((TargetFilename LIKE '%\\inetpub\\wwwroot\\aspnet\_client\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\FrontEnd\\HttpProxy\\owa\\auth\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\FrontEnd\\HttpProxy\\ecp\\auth\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\HttpProxy\\OAB\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (TargetFilename LIKE '%.aspx' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%.ashx' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%.asmx' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Exchange Web Shell Dropped to OWA/ECP Auth Path

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Security 4663 ReadData access to an ntds.dit file, on the live NTDS path or inside a shadow copy device path, by a process other than lsass and the allowlisted backup engines. Every offline NTDS theft that goes through the file system (ntdsutil IFM, esentutl or copy from a shadow copy, robocopy /b, backup-privilege readers) has to open the file, whatever its command line says.
falsepositives: Documented IFM media creation for DC promotion by Tier-0 admins (ntdsutil.exe)
Third-party system-state backup agents not yet listed in filter_expected_readers
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4663 AND ObjectName LIKE '%\\ntds.dit' ESCAPE '\') AND (AccessMask='0x1' OR AccessList LIKE '%\%\%4416%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\wbengine.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_BACKUP\_AGENT\_IMAGE' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: NTDS.dit File Read by Unexpected Process (4663)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects SID History manipulation. The primary attack signal is a write to the sIDHistory attribute (Directory Service Changes 5136), made by Mimikatz sid::add (after sid::patch) or ADMT-style DsAddSidHistory. Windows also emits 4765 (SID History added) and 4766 (add failed) during ADMT migration; both are included as a secondary signal. Two related techniques are not visible here. DCShadow pushes sIDHistory through replication from a rogue DC and avoids 5136 (see dcshadow_replication_rpcserver), and "kerberos::golden /sids:<RootDomainSID-519>" (the PDF reference) places ExtraSids in a forged ticket without writing sIDHistory at all. The 5136 branch fires at critical when the added value is a privileged well-known RID (500 Administrator, 512 Domain Admins, 516 Domain Controllers, 518 Schema Admins, 519 Enterprise Admins) of any domain, including the forest root, or Builtin Administrators. Other sIDHistory additions are sid_history_attribute_write at high, and value deletions (post-migration clean-up) no longer alert.
falsepositives: Genuine cross-domain migration via ADMT (must be ticketed and rare)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=5136 AND AttributeLDAPDisplayName='sIDHistory' AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\') AND (AttributeValue REGEXP 'S-1-5-21-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-(500|512|516|518|519)([^0-9]|$)' OR AttributeValue LIKE '%S-1-5-32-544%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (EventID=4765 OR EventID=4766))
title: SID History Added to Account (Forest/Domain Privilege Escalation)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects Netlogon event 5829: a vulnerable Netlogon secure channel connection was allowed because the DC is not yet in enforcement mode or the client is on the allow list. This is the only Netlogon event that indicates an exploitable Zerologon path was actually used. Denied connections (5827/5828) and policy-allowed connections (5830/5831) are inventory signals and live in zerologon_netlogon_denied_or_allowed_by_policy.yml. The DC computer-account password-reset corroborator is zerologon_dc_account_password_null.yml. PDF reference: "cve-2020-1472-exploit.py" then secretsdump.
falsepositives: Legacy devices using vulnerable Netlogon (investigate each; should be rare post-patch)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND EventID=5829
title: Vulnerable Netlogon Secure Channel Allowed (Zerologon CVE-2020-1472 Exploitable Path)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of known Mimikatz support files in System32: mimidrv.sys, mimilib.dll, kiwissp.log. Requires Sysmon EID 11.
falsepositives: Unlikely
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=11 AND (TargetFilename LIKE '%\\mimidrv.sys' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\mimilib.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\kiwissp.log' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetFilename LIKE '%\\System32\\kiwissp.log' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Mimikatz Driver or SSP DLL Dropped to System32

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a password reset (4724), a password change (4723) or any account change (4738) on the krbtgt account or on an RODC krbtgt account, which is named krbtgt_<number>. Should only happen as part of the documented twice-reset hygiene procedure or after a suspected Golden Ticket. An attacker who sets the krbtgt key to a known value (Mimikatz lsadump::setntlm or lsadump::changentlm) can forge tickets without having to dump it; an RODC krbtgt key forges tickets that the RODC accepts and that writable DCs honour for accounts in the RODC's allowed list. PDF reference: krbtgt hash dumped via lsadump::dcsync.
falsepositives: Scheduled krbtgt rotation (must be ticketed and rare)
RODC promotion, which creates and sets the RODC's krbtgt_<number> account
Microsoft Entra Kerberos server key rotation, which resets krbtgt_AzureAD
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4723 OR EventID=4724 OR EventID=4738) AND (TargetUserName='krbtgt' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'krbtgt\_%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: krbtgt Account Password Reset

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a Kerberos TGT issued without pre-authentication (4768 PreAuthType 0) for the decoy AS-REP account, a user account deliberately configured with "Do not require Kerberos preauthentication" and used by nothing. The AS-REP it returns is encrypted with the account key, so a request means someone is AS-REP roasting (Rubeus asreproast, Impacket GetNPUsers, NetExec --asreproast) and has collected a hash to crack offline.
falsepositives: AD assessment tools that request an AS-REP for every account without pre-authentication to prove it is roastable. Tell the assessment team the decoy exists or exclude it from their scope.
An administrator testing the decoy after setting it up. Test before the placeholder is substituted.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 AND PreAuthType=0) AND (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_ASREP\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_ASREP\_ACCOUNT@%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Honeytoken AS-REP Account TGT Issued Without Pre-Authentication

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects registration of a Security Support Provider by modification of the LSA "Security Packages" or "OSConfig\Security Packages" registry values. A malicious SSP (mimilib, custom DLL) is loaded into LSASS at next boot and records cleartext credentials. The in-memory variant (mimikatz misc::memssp) leaves no registry write; its command line is covered by mimikatz_indicators.yml and its file artefacts (kiwissp.log, mimilib.dll) by mimikatz_driver_or_ssp_dll_drop.yml. This rule was split from a mixed-source rule whose file and command-line branches could never match a registry event.
falsepositives: Vendor SSP installation (rare, must be documented)
Windows servicing writing the default package list (filter on Image being TiWorker.exe or msiexec.exe after baselining)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\Lsa\\Security Packages%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Control\\Lsa\\OSConfig\\Security Packages%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((Details='(Empty)' OR Details='""'), 0))))
title: Custom SSP Registered via Security Packages Registry Value

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects setting of HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\DsrmAdminLogonBehavior to value 2 which enables the DSRM administrator account to log on as a normal domain admin. PDF reference: "PowerShell New-ItemProperty ... DsrmAdminLogonBehavior -Value 2".
falsepositives: Documented DC recovery procedures (should be exceptional and ticketed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational' AND (EventID=13 AND (TargetObject LIKE '%CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Lsa\\DsrmAdminLogonBehavior%' ESCAPE '\' AND (Details='DWORD (0x00000002)' OR Details=2)))
title: DSRM Admin Logon Behavior Enabled (Persistence Backdoor)

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects any authentication attempt, successful or failed, for a decoy user account that no person or service uses: a Kerberos TGT request (4768), Kerberos pre-authentication failure (4771), NTLM credential validation (4776), logon success or failure (4624, 4625) or explicit-credential logon (4648). The decoys are the two honey users, the honey Kerberoast account and the honey AS-REP account. Any of these events means someone holds or is guessing the decoy's credentials: a password spray that swept the decoy, a cracked Kerberoast or AS-REP hash being used, or a planted credential (for example the cpassword in the decoy GPP file) being tried.
falsepositives: Unlikely once the decoys are set up as the README describes. Nothing legitimate should authenticate as a decoy.

The single bootstrap logon an administrator performs to give the decoy a realistic lastLogonTimestamp, if it is done after the rule is deployed. Do it before substituting the placeholder, and never schedule repeat logons.
Authorised penetration tests and password audits that spray every account. Treat the alert as a true positive for the tester's activity and confirm the source address with the test lead.
A user who mistypes a user name close to a decoy name. Choose decoy names that are not one keystroke away from a real account.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4768 OR EventID=4771 OR EventID=4776 OR EventID=4624 OR EventID=4625 OR EventID=4648) AND (((TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_USER01' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_USER02' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_KERBEROAST\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_USER01@%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_USER02@%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_KERBEROAST\_ACCOUNT@%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_ASREP\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_HONEY\_ASREP\_ACCOUNT@%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((EventID=4768 AND PreAuthType=0), 0)))))
title: Honeytoken User Authentication Attempt

author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects a write to nTSecurityDescriptor on the domain root object (objectClass domainDNS). This is the outcome of PrivExchange and of any ntlmrelayx --escalate-user relay to LDAP, which grants the attacker Replication (DCSync) rights on the domain. Domain-root DACL changes are rare and should always be ticketed. The Exchange EWS push-subscription request that triggers PrivExchange is covered by the IIS rule privexchange_ews_push_subscription.yml. author: 404secnotfound
description: Detects creation of a Delegated Managed Service Account or a write to its predecessor-link attribute, the basis of the Windows Server 2025 dMSA "BadSuccessor" privilege-escalation technique now in active eCrime use. Creation of a dMSA (5137), and writes to the two attributes that decide who may use it (msDS-GroupMSAMembership, the principals allowed to retrieve its password, and nTSecurityDescriptor), are suppressed only for the positive allowlist of dMSA administrators, so the BadSuccessor precondition (a user holding only CreateChild on an OU creating a dMSA there and granting itself retrieval) alerts. A write to the predecessor link or migration state alerts whoever makes it. Other attribute changes on a dMSA object, which the DC makes on its own, are out of scope. The read and use steps are dmsa_managed_password_read and dmsa_authentication_unexpected_host.
falsepositives: Sanctioned dMSA deployment on Server 2025 by an account not yet listed in filter_dmsa_admins (rare, ticketed)

Sanctioned service-account migration with Start-ADServiceAccountMigration, which writes the predecessor link (ticketed). [Inference] During that migration the DC may also grant the migrating host password retrieval on the dMSA (msDS-GroupMSAMembership) under its own account; that write is part of the same ticketed change.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((((EventID=5137 AND ObjectClass='msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount') OR (EventID=5136 AND ObjectClass='msDS-DelegatedManagedServiceAccount' AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-GroupMSAMembership' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='nTSecurityDescriptor') AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE 'PLACEHOLDER\_DMSA\_ADMIN\_ACCOUNT' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR (EventID=5136 AND (AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink' OR AttributeLDAPDisplayName='msDS-DelegatedMSAState') AND OperationType LIKE '\%\%14674' ESCAPE '\'))
title: dMSA BadSuccessor Abuse (Delegated Managed Service Account)
